title: macOS LaunchAgent runs Zerus at daemon priority; CPU load starves the GUI until the watchdog aborts it
description: hgs-tray 0.42.2 on macOS 27 froze completely under 10 niced busy loops while other apps stayed responsive; after 30 s MainThreadWatchdog aborted it (crash 2026-10-15 14:19:39, main thread incidentally inside ActivityBrowser::paintEvent). Root cause: tray/packaging/com.hgdev.hgs-tray.plist has no ProcessType, so launchd spawns it as 'spawn type = daemon (3)' and clamps every thread to priority 20, below default-priority load (31) even when that load is niced. A thread QoS request from inside the process stays clamped at 20. Measured with launchd probes under 12 nice-0 busy loops: 2 ms CPU chunk p99 134 ms (daemon) vs 6.6 ms (ProcessType=Interactive) vs 4.7 ms (Interactive + USER_INTERACTIVE main-thread QoS). Fix: ProcessType=Interactive in the plist template, USER_INTERACTIVE QoS for the macOS GUI thread, docs for existing Homebrew autostart installs.
notes:
Verified on the live tray: same binary with only ProcessType=Interactive in the installed plist survived 45 s of 10 x nice-19 busy loops and 30 s of 12 x nice-0 busy loops; main thread PRI 31, 8-40% CPU, no watchdog line, no crash report (before: PRI 20, ~1.5% CPU, abort at 30 s). Branch fix/ui-hang-under-load in <project checkout>
Installed on the owner's Mac via tray/install.sh from fix/ui-hang-under-load (7743b87 + uncommitted fix): spawn type interactive, GUI thread PRI 37, workers 31; survived 45 s 10 x nice-19 + 30 s 12 x nice-0 busy loops without abort. Tests: 63/63 GUI ctest, test_macos_setup/bundle/tray_update/mac_install, check-source.py. Not committed yet (awaiting owner).

Verified live on the owner's Mac (spawn type interactive, GUI thread 37, survived 75 s of 10-12 busy loops without watchdog abort); retained unchanged in 7a6274b with fully green CI run 38740582425 (macOS desktop, Arch desktop, CLI macos-15 green). title: Windows desktops whose whole session is in a job cannot start local sessions
description: Reported 2026-10-17 (Zerus 0.44.0, hgs 1.53.0, Windows 11 Home 26H2 build 26300): every process of the interactive session, explorer.exe included, is in a job; hgs-tray.exe started from Explorer cannot start a host (ClientError::InJob). CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB succeeds but the child stays in a job, so an outer job forbids breakaway. D4 refuses a host in any job, so local sessions never start on such a desktop. Proposal (needs the reporter's job data first): accept a host whose own job also holds the desktop shell (GetShellWindow's process in JobObjectBasicProcessIdList), since such sessions then end no earlier than the desktop, which docs already state; keep refusing every other job (agent sandboxes, terminals, CI steps). Also name the remedy in the desktop error, and review that the GUI's PTY and swarm-worker kill-on-close jobs lack BREAKAWAY_OK.
close_reason: Merged in #203 (29dc8a0f): a host whose job also holds the desktop shell is accepted (desktop_job); reproduced and verified on the Windows dev PC. GUI PTY and swarm-worker jobs follow in zerus-tft0.

Next step: finish the brainstorming for #0 with the owner (questions below, one at a time), present the design, write docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-16-ios-foundation-design.md, get owner review, then writing-plans.

Environment verified 2026-10-16: arm64 Mac, macOS 27.0.1, Xcode 27.0 (27A266a), iOS 26.0 simulator runtime. Test iPhone 11 Pro on iOS 26.0 is paired and connected (xcrun devicectl list devices). A valid Apple Development certificate of the owner's paid team is in the login keychain and Xcode has an Apple ID account, so automatic signing with -allowProvisioningUpdates should work. A Developer ID Application certificate exists for macOS casks; there is no Apple Distribution certificate yet (needed by #9). xcodegen, fastlane and tuist are not installed; Homebrew lives in /opt/homebrew and is only on the login-shell PATH (use zsh -lc over ssh). About 54 GB disk free (88 percent used): keep DerivedData in one dedicated bounded location.

Open questions for the owner:
(a) Bundle ID, durable once an App Store record exists. Candidate: app.zerus.mobile, identical to the Android applicationId, one app ID shared by Dev/TestFlight/Stable as Android shares one package.
(b) Minimum iOS version. Proposal: iOS 17.
(c) Meaning of Dev. Proposal: a locally built, development-signed build installed on the attached iPhone by a script; TestFlight internal testing becomes the Dev channel in #9.

Proposed design (not yet approved):
- mobile/ios/Zerus.xcodeproj using Xcode file-system synchronized groups (objectVersion 77), so the project file stays small and new sources are picked up from folders; no generator dependency.
- A SwiftUI app target, a testable core module (protocol models, RelayClient, credential store) and unit tests runnable on the simulator.
- mobile/ios/DEV_VERSION (marketing base) plus a build number from the CI sequence; local builds embed source commit and dirty state and never claim a CI number.
- mobile/ios/scripts/dev-install.sh on the Mac: xcodebuild with automatic signing and -allowProvisioningUpdates, dedicated -derivedDataPath, install with xcrun devicectl device install app, launch with devicectl device process launch. A Linux-side wrapper rsyncs a worktree's mobile/ios to a Mac scratch directory over ssh -o BatchMode=yes and runs it, so agents on Arch can build uncommitted work.
- Walking skeleton: pairing (POST /v1/pair, credential in Keychain, HTTPS only, zerus://pair link prefill with explicit confirmation), GET /v1/capabilities, GET /v1/computers list, and the read-only demo.
- CI: a macOS job on a standard runner that builds for the simulator without signing and runs the unit tests, wired into the existing ci.yml gate.
- Docs: mobile/ios/README.md (build and install), README.md mobile section, docs/mobile-architecture.md status line.
notes: 2026-10-16: foundation merged to main via PR #185 (merge 3eb4da5c, CI gate success including the new ios job). Simulator verified. Remaining for this task: install on the test iPhone once Xcode on the Mac has a signed-in Apple ID of the team (or an App Store Connect API key is provided); then dev-install.sh needs no further changes.
close_reason: 2026-10-17: Release Dev build from main installed and launched on the test iPhone with automatic signing through the team's existing Developer-role App Store Connect API key (the notarization key; no Xcode account needed). Xcode registered app.zerus.mobile with Push Notifications. Found and fixed on device: local Release builds are development-signed, so the APNs environment now follows the build channel (local = sandbox). On-device checks of recording, playback and push remain with the owner's first use.

title: iOS client with Android feature parity (native SwiftUI)
description:
Goal (owner, 2026-10-16): build the iOS version of the Zerus mobile client, learn to build and install Dev builds on the test iPhone attached to the Mac, then produce TestFlight/App Store builds.

Owner decisions from the 2026-10-16 brainstorming (superpowers brainstorming, architectural path):
1. Scope: full feature parity with the Android client, not an MVP.
2. Approach A: a separate native Swift/SwiftUI client under mobile/ios. Port logic from the Kotlin client; do not refactor Android. Keep subtle contracts aligned with shared JSON contract fixtures exercised by both Android and iOS tests (existing examples: mobile/android/app/src/test/resources/session-filter-contract.json and optional-question-contract.json). Rejected: B (Kotlin Multiplatform shared logic + SwiftUI) and C (Compose Multiplatform); both require restructuring the working Android app.
3. Decompose into sub-projects; each gets its own spec, plan and implementation (brainstorming -> written spec in docs/superpowers/specs -> owner review -> writing-plans -> execution). Order: #0 foundation and Dev build, then #9 TestFlight/App Store distribution immediately after #0, then #1 sessions and machines, #2 conversation, #3-#7 in parallel, #8 notifications.

State at handoff: classification, scope, approach and decomposition are approved. The #0 design is not yet approved; its open questions are listed in the #0 child. No spec, plan or code exists yet.

Reading list: docs/mobile-architecture.md (Protocol version 1 table, Trust and authorization, Delivery safety, Notifications, Public distribution), services/mobile/relay/README.md, mobile/android/README.md, mobile/android/app/src/main/java/app/zerus/mobile/ (about 20k lines; RelayApi.kt, ZerusViewModel.kt, MainActivity.kt are the entry points), mobile/android/app/src/test, docs/public-distribution.md (Dev version rule), docs/macos-distribution.md (Apple credentials, macos-signing environment), docs/ci-and-aur.md, CONTRIBUTING.md.

Constraints (AGENTS.md): keep API v1 and durable request identities compatible; no credentials or login material in the repository; free standard GitHub runners only; SHA-pinned actions; Apple credentials stay in the main-only macos-signing environment; never auto-merge; mirror instruction changes in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md; Dev builds use next-version-dev.N.

iOS-specific facts: CFBundleShortVersionString must be at most three integers, so the -dev.N suffix cannot be part of the marketing version; carry the Dev sequence in CFBundleVersion and show X.Y.Z-dev.N in About. The relay accepts only provider fcm in POST /v1/push today; iOS needs APNs either directly from the relay or through FCM for iOS (decide in #8). The Android in-app updater does not apply on iOS; distribution is TestFlight/App Store.
Unassigned so far: Firebase diagnostics and usage analytics parity (docs/mobile-architecture.md Firebase diagnostics) and third-party notices; decide during #9 together with the privacy manifest.

title: Track explicit waits between independent agent sessions
description: Owner requests explicit cross-provider independent-session waiting with awaiting acknowledgement and awaiting result phases. Persist exact waiter and producer identities plus request correlation through hgs; settle only matching acknowledgement/result or cancellation, never from prose or peer idleness. Keep waiting sessions in Active, display producer and elapsed wait in desktop and Android, and show a dashed amber Graph relation. Preserve native work/attention priority, request no-replay identities, bounded indexed storage and API-v1 compatibility. Commit and push the qualified implementation and verify CI.
design: Explicit declarations bind an exact waiter run/conversation and a producer portable reference. Native callers reuse verified process ancestry; operators and API-host agents use a checked local waiter reference, visibly authored coordination rather than inferred native work. Scoped private reply tickets authorize acknowledgement and finish. Finish additionally verifies the original waiting computer own successful native result-send receipt, exact run/conversation and time after declaration. State and idempotent operations are transactional in a private indexed SQLite journal; permanent UUID tombstones survive 30-day detail expiry. Listings use one read snapshot, per-owner revisions, exact counts and four-record previews; journal pages use immutable seq keysets. Desktop/Android defer reply-only completion while explicitly waiting, preserving work and attention priority. Graph derives dashed amber edges from bounded current metadata and exact known native endpoint matches. Protocol documented in docs/agent-coordination.md and mirrored in AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md.
notes:

title: Claude child StopFailure keeps the parent Working forever
description: A Claude workflow child that ends with StopFailure (for example rate_limit 'weekly limit') is saved as state=working with display_state=unknown and never receives SubagentStop. Counters report it as unknown (subagent_active_count 0), but telemetry::child_working() checks only state==working, so Stop and settle_children keep the parent phase=working and all idle-only actions (pause, fork, effort, clear, compact) stay blocked. Observed 2026-10-16 on arch: session builds idle at the native prompt since its end_turn, shown as Working for 15+ hours; the workflow journal records type=failed for that agent and its transcript ends with a synthetic isApiErrorMessage rate_limit row. Needs owner direction on status semantics: proposal is to settle the child as finished with an error outcome when the hook reports StopFailure or the workflow journal records failed, and never let an unknown child establish current work.
close_reason: Merged in PR #184 (3120b6f8): Claude child StopFailure or workflow failure settles as error; unknown children never keep the parent working; stale records repaired on read.

title: Swarm controller loops on run_groups and disables conflict review
description: Commit 7406d595 added run_groups to SessionOrganization::toJson(), but SwarmController::presentation() copies only default_project, runs and imported_machines from the local organization. Every SessionsWindow rebuild re-adds run_groups through observe(), saveOrganization() calls SwarmController::edit(), m_desired differs from m_base, the controller sends a no-op swarm apply, presentation() drops run_groups again and organizationReady triggers another rebuild. Observed on mac Dev773 (2026-10-16): the persisted swarm/observedOrganization lacks run_groups while workspace/organization has it, and only 'hgs swarm apply' calls (no 5 s polls) were seen. Because settled() is false most of the time, SwarmDialog calls review->setBusy(true) every 200 ms and the conflict choices table is disabled, so the owner cannot select a value. The round trip also wipes run_groups, so archived run placement can be lost. Fix: preserve run_groups as local-only data in presentation() and add a regression test that a rebuild with run_groups settles without apply.
close_reason: Merged in PR #183 (f3590735): SwarmController::presentation keeps run_groups, so Sessions rebuilds no longer loop through swarm apply and conflict choices stay selectable.

title: Mobile delivery fixture test leaves account refreshes running and hangs Python 3.12 teardown
description: CI #721 (0d962407) Rust relay job hit its 25-minute deadline: after test_only_the_gateway_advertises_and_its_snapshot_reports_the_value printed ok, asyncio logged 'Close running child process: kill' and unittest never continued. Reproduced locally with CPython 3.12.13 and the CI package install: every snapshot starts an AccountCache.refresh task; the test closed only the journal, so IsolatedAsyncioTestCase teardown cancelled refresh, create_subprocess_exec and the transport's _connect_pipes together; the spawn cleanup then waits forever in Runner._cancel_all_tasks for an exit that needs connected pipes. Fix: await the peer and root AccountCache.close() before closing the journal, as Connector.run shutdown and other connector tests do.

title: Start the shared tmux server outside the unit that first needs it
description: Found by the zerus-nbzl.2 rehearsal (2026-10-15, systemd 262, tmux 3.8 built with libsystemd): tmux puts every pane created by a client inside a systemd unit into a tmux-spawn-<uuid>.scope with PartOf=<the unit holding the tmux server> and SendSIGHUP=yes. When that unit is stopped, systemd also stops these pane scopes, so the tmux server exits after its last pane, even with KillMode=process. Whatever unit first starts the shared default tmux server (a desktop-launched GUI unit, hgs-tray.service, zerus-mobile-connector.service, a worker) therefore owns all agent panes: stopping it, or a graphical logout when it is PartOf graphical-session.target, can end every native agent. Start the shared tmux server in its own transient scope (systemd-run --user --scope, as the DeepSeek and opencode hosts already do) whenever hgs has to create it, verify with systemctl --user show -p ConsistsOf, and rehearse only on isolated tmux sockets. Never restart or stop live units to test this.
notes: PR #126 (fix/tmux-server-own-scope), reviewed; awaiting CI.
close_reason: Merged in PR #126: on Linux inside a user unit with a reachable user manager, hgs starts a new shared tmux server in its own hgs-tmux-<uuid> scope (systemd-run --user --scope --collect), so stopping the launching unit no longer ends agent panes; running servers are never touched; refused scopes fall back to the plain command. CI ran the new integration test on ubuntu-24.04 (3 pass, PartOf control skipped: runner tmux lacks systemd).

description: Owner decision 2026-10-15: «переписывай мобильный коннектор на рст». Current nbzl.6/.7/.8/.9 and 3rqx.2 trees have no in-flight runtime edits to protocol.rs/context.py/connector.py/mobile_peers.rs at this inspection; their test/crate work remains active and unfrozen. zerus-stlj (Android file links, codex/zerus/zerus-dev, branch fix/android-computer-file-links) adds a read-only file_read operation: hgs file-read <session> --json snapshot (<=10 MiB), connector chunks <=512 KiB with sha256 for later chunks and a 120 s cache, relay short-retention index like attachment_read, and a new connector journal index file_delivered_reads (vectors/journal/*.sql regenerated). The Rust connector must keep it: C1 accepts/creates that index in place (IF NOT EXISTS, rollback-compatible both ways), C2 recognises the native capability marker, C4 ports file_read with a black-box suite. Preferred order: zerus-stlj merges before C1; otherwise C1 adds the index.
file_read parity checklist (zerus-stlj frozen source 91c389a9, services/mobile/zerus_mobile/file_reads.py): operation file_read in READS but not READ_SQL; native capability gate HELP_MARKER 'file-read <session> --json'; payload request_id/expected_run_id/expected_conversation_id/path (+ optional archive_id, agent_id), offset/length with length <= 512 KiB (MAX_READ_BYTES) and offset+length <= 10 MiB (MAX_FILE_BYTES); first read without digest, later ranges only with the original sha256 (cache hit or verified reread); per original machine context snapshot cache 30 MiB / 120 s; connector journal index file_delivered_reads (CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS, 120 s delivered-read retention); relay file_history index (60 s, 5 s read grace). Golden vectors on main after zerus-stlj merges cover validation, envelopes, execution projections, missing path, C1 controls, UTF-8 byte caps, later-range digest and archive/child. Port in C4 with a black-box suite; no migration blocker found (verified read-only 2026-10-15). Deploy note for the root integrator: the relay creates file_history at startup without CONCURRENTLY; the short-retention requests table keeps the lock brief.

title: Recognize Claude tool-use interruption before gating context actions
description: Read-only investigation on 2026-10-15 reproduced a disabled Compact and continue and Clear context while the native Claude parent showed a completed turn and empty prompt. Parent main_done=true and no active tools; one workflow child remained working. Its exact owned native tail is a user/external text row [Request interrupted by user for tool use] following an error tool result. src/state/claude_subagents.rs recognizes only [Request interrupted by user], so the tool-use variant falls through to user_message and reclassifies the interrupted child as working. title: Prevent default Inbox observation from racing explicit project assignment
description: A newly observed session can be published into the local default project while another desktop explicitly assigns the same exact machine/session to its selected project. Verified catalog history contains two concurrent parentless session assignments at the same clock: the observing host chose ungrouped while the launching desktop chose the selected project. A later explicit write merged both parents and restored the intended project. Passive observation must not compete with an explicit launch or move. Preserve deliberate moves to the default project, exact launch/run/session identity, existing conflict review and compatibility with resident clients. Add a synthetic two-peer regression before choosing the protocol or presentation fix.
design: Keep first-observed session rows and their order in the local desktop organization with an unassigned_sessions marker. SwarmController removes those memberships from both initialize and apply payloads; explicit moves and verified launches remove the marker. Shared catalog membership wins over passive placement on refresh, including rename arrival ordering. New payloads carry the additive organization hint session_assignments_explicit so the CLI preserves unseen competing explicit choices instead of applying its legacy passive-observation guard. Older CLIs ignore that hint; shared operation schema, existing assignments/conflicts and unmarked historical caches are unchanged. Full race prevention requires updating observing desktops; the CLI update additionally preserves explicit first-choice conflicts.
acceptance_criteria: A remote session launched into an explicit project remains in that project when another GUI first observes it concurrently; passive fallback display does not create an authoritative competing assignment. Explicit moves to the default project remain synchronized. Existing and real conflicts are preserved for review.
notes:
2026-10-12 validation: the new desktop regression failed before the fix by exporting passive session membership. The fixed source passes all 53 Linux GUI targets and all 15 affected native macOS targets, 27 Swarm unit contracts on Rust 1.85, and 15 isolated real-CLI Swarm tests (14-suite run plus the added compatibility contract). Both observation/launch write orders converge without assignment conflicts; an unseen explicit first choice remains a reviewable conflict. The additive hint also passes against the retained pre-fix CLI binary without changing catalog operations. Source privacy/syntax/version checks and targeted rustfmt pass.
2026-10-12 final integration: the Inbox fix and composer feedback cleanup are reconciled with main 944f19e. Full Linux GUI build and all 53 CTest targets pass; native macOS GUI build and all 15 final integration targets pass, with all 314 staged GUI/build/test source files verified by SHA-256.

title: Remove blocking draft writer barriers from navigation and send UI
description: Review zerus-pta0 against retained 0.41.0 release source: ComposerDraftStore::load and keys call global flushWrites; DraftWrites::flush and sync use BlockingQueuedConnection without a deadline. New-session selection, Saved drafts and explicit sending can therefore block the GUI behind unrelated slow disk writes despite asynchronous typing. A synthetic 400 ms writer delay makes loading an unrelated absent draft block the main thread 410 ms (0.13 ms thread CPU); queued GUI work cannot run. Use asynchronous draft loading and durable-send continuation with operation identity and fresh validation. Preserve atomic persistence before transport, draft recovery and no replay; do not bypass the durable barrier. Test navigation and explicit send while the writer remains stalled. Existing typing responsiveness coverage releases the writer before its send assertion.
design: Use one ordered worker with coalesced edit snapshots and noncoalescing durable operations. All GUI reads/index scans/writes use asynchronous continuations with exact key and revision. Loading may lock only its composer; navigation remains responsive. Pin accepted payload and target identity before durability, prevent duplicate sends, revalidate before transport, preserve recovery and no replay. Persist rename destination before retiring source. Normal widget destruction never globally drains; graceful application shutdown may drain.
notes: Implemented and reviewed asynchronous draft load/index/rename, ordered durable submission continuations, and bounded background attachment preparation/retry reads. Accepted payloads stay pinned to their original target across navigation; stale identity, failed persistence, missing retry receipt and expired unconsented cache prevent dispatch. Tests hold storage blocked while proving event-loop progress, navigation and zero premature transport; 22 integration outcome rows pass, including native Cocoa. Composer, question, attachment and SessionsWindow suites pass on macOS and Arch. User-selected attachment import remains synchronous within the reviewed scope. Qualified source change; installed GUI not updated.
close_reason: Implemented, independently reviewed and qualified on macOS and Linux; source changes are ready for review, without deployment.

title: Bound Activity rendering latency and defer hidden transcript layout
description: Review zerus-pta0: ActivityView::render regenerates HTML and synchronously replaces and fully lays out the whole QTextDocument after one changed reply (ActivityView.cpp:1254-1264). SessionsWindow calls setTimeline even when Activity is hidden. Release Qt offscreen synthetic approximately 1 KB replies: 100 replies take 125-126 ms per change; 250 take 297-299 ms; 500 take 587-596 ms; hidden 500-reply updates take 580 ms. Identical snapshots are below 0.2 ms. This blocks all input on the shared GUI event loop. Implement bounded/incremental visible transcript work and defer hidden rendering while keeping data current. Preserve reading anchors, selection, exact history, clear boundaries and delivery identities. Add meaningful event-loop latency qualification for changed long histories and hidden panels; average idle CPU is insufficient.
design: Prepare journal HTML, source QTextDocument layout, cloned browser text and cursor-line geometry on one low-priority job per view. Qt setDocument invalidates an ordinary prepared document, so install a public QAbstractTextDocumentLayout adapter delegating draw, hit testing and geometry to the owned immutable source document; map selections by identical text positions and preserve image cursor metrics. Keep one active job plus the latest pending input. Separate presentation epochs from content revisions so same-conversation streaming makes progress without accepting stale session, search, theme or geometry results. Hidden views defer work. Commit preserves current selection and reading anchors. Each dedicated job thread parks after preparation until its document tree is retired: Qt FreeType destroys thread-local faces on thread exit despite live layout references, and sharing a working renderer thread with GUI paint could race font-engine caches. At application shutdown, drain preparation, delete documents while font resources remain alive, then stop and join threads before Qt GUI global teardown. Validate bounded thread retirement, interaction contracts and main-thread gaps through first paint, not setter time alone.
notes: Implemented and reviewed in isolated source worktree based on d8ceeab. HTML, full layout and cursor geometry run off the GUI thread; immutable layout adapter preserves selection, links and full history. Dedicated workers park until document retirement to preserve FreeType thread-local faces, with at most two workers per view. Hidden views defer work and streaming coalesces without starvation. Native Cocoa 500-reply changed snapshots: 21-27 ms GUI gaps including first paint, 1.18-1.26 s background preparation. Activity and SessionsWindow suites pass on macOS Qt 6.11.2 and Arch Qt 6.12.0. ASAN passes on both, including bounded worker retirement, pending shutdown and a separate live installed-document shutdown harness. Qualified source change; installed GUI not updated.
close_reason: Implemented, independently reviewed and qualified on macOS and Linux; source changes are ready for review, without deployment.

title: Review desktop UI stalls under host load after performance fixes
description: Analyze main-thread responsiveness under general computer load, verify the installed version and remaining synchronous rendering or I/O paths, collect passive profiles and isolated synthetic measurements, and record prioritized findings. Audit only; preserve live native agents and user drafts.
notes:
Verified 2026-10-11: the live macOS process reports 0.41.0 and has a zerus-draft-writer thread; the checkout is 0.40.0 (05f0729). Reviewed the retained 0.41.0 release source archive. ActivityView.cpp and SessionList.cpp are byte-identical across the checkout and archive. Exact installed binary provenance is unconfirmed: its Mach-O UUID differs from the retained release build. An 8-second passive sample captures ActivityView::render -> setHtml/documentSize and whole-list/card painting on the main thread; fsync for ordinary draft edits is on the writer thread. No sustained total hang was captured. Isolated Release/Qt offscreen measurements with synthetic approximately 1 KB replies: changing one reply blocks setActivity for 125-126 ms with 100 replies, 297-299 ms with 250, and 587-596 ms with 500. Hidden Activity still costs 580 ms with 500 replies. Identical snapshots cost below 0.2 ms. With the existing write observer delaying only the draft worker 400 ms, loading an unrelated absent draft blocks the main thread 410 ms with only 0.13 ms thread CPU; a queued event does not run until return. Eight synthetic active rows at 2x scale repaint 25 times in two seconds (32 ms thread CPU); disabling activity animation produces zero paints in the same static fixture. These establish defects and avoidable work, not a complete attribution of the reported live freeze. Local diagnostic artifacts: /tmp/zerus-ui-review-harness and /tmp/zerus-ui-review-sample.txt. No application source edits, GUI/native restarts, live stress or publication.
Prioritized follow-ups: zerus-nug6 (P1 bounded Activity and hidden rendering), zerus-ts35 (P1 asynchronous draft barriers), zerus-3onx (P2 animation repaint regions). Review complete; the original live-load symptom remains unqualified until these paths are fixed and event-loop/input latency is measured under representative CPU and I/O pressure.
User clarified after the initial review: macOS; the entire interface stalls, including scrolling, switching sessions and all UI actions; typing makes the symptom especially apparent. This is a whole-window responsiveness report, not merely slow backend/session updates.
Typing-path follow-up, 2026-10-11: in retained 0.41.0 source, text/cursor signals enqueue asynchronous saves; draftChanged rebuilds the list only when draft presence changes, not on every character. The existing live sample also captures saveAsync -> directory -> QSettings construction -> QMacSettingsPrivate::sync -> CFPreferences on the GUI thread. This is residual native-settings work, not a demonstrated stall: 1000 synthetic native-format directory lookups measured median 0.0095 ms, p99 0.0147 ms and maximum 0.0868 ms. Do not attribute the reported freeze to this call without slow-episode evidence. The P1 Activity and blocking draft-barrier findings remain the strongest reproduced problems.

title: Deliver main-based dev updates with bounded build retention
description: Owner request 2026-10-11: deliver new main features to desktop computers and Android without repeated manual build updates, while preventing uncontrolled growth in GitHub Releases. Current source already exposes Android dev and desktop stable/nightly discovery, but Android publication is manual, nightly is daily and Linux-only, desktop automatic discovery is throttled to 24 hours, and desktop has no installer. design: Owner clarified 2026-10-11: automate publication and notifications only for now; Android must have its own dev update channel. Implement successful-main dev artifact delivery and client discovery with bounded storage; no automatic installer or download. Keep GitHub Releases for existing stable/nightly contracts and use Actions artifacts for per-main dev candidates served anonymously by the verified public mirror. Introduce an additive dev catalog v2 with exact run and source provenance while retaining old dev Android catalog compatibility for already-installed clients during bootstrap. Current signing and macOS credential prerequisites must be surfaced honestly. Do not delete or overwrite existing GitHub releases.
acceptance_criteria: A successful upstream-main build can advance a dev channel automatically; failed, cancelled, stale or foreign runs cannot replace its current build. Distribution covers Android and actual desktop installable formats, preserves signing/application identity, drafts and live native agents, and includes explicit bounded retention. title: Investigate intermittent process history cache recovery failure during release qualification
description: Release candidate 38142162351, exact source 9b8463dddfef568925c6795d538d5cafd8266e63: Linux Rust unit test state::processes::history::tests::incremental_recovery_caches_exact_completion_and_rejects_other_conversation failed at history.rs:227. notes: Verified reproduction: a concurrent child fork inherits the raw history-lock file descriptor, so closing the parent descriptor can leave the same flock alive until the child execs/exits. title: Confirm cold context before submitting native question answers

design: Astra design: Desktop and Android native question answers use an explicit cold-cache cost choice before any sending state or transport. Capture the exact target, run/conversation, question identity/source/tool/schema, emitted answer payload and raw saved form/draft state. Revalidate identity, availability, unchanged draft and no existing pending/submitted/uncertain delivery after consent; same-schema polling is allowed. Guard reentrant dialogs and duplicate sends. Android retains only an in-memory confirmation intent across rotation, drops it on process restart and enforces the gate centrally in ViewModel.send so inline, expanded, approval and skip paths cannot bypass it. Preserve native no-replay receipts and exact form replacement mechanics.
notes: Implemented and Astra-reviewed the desktop and Android common question-send cold-cache consent gates. title: Start hgs subprocesses without blocking the GUI thread
description: runHgs in tray/src/HgsClient.cpp starts about one hgs child per second (local ls every 2 s, peer ls over ssh, git-status, inspect, recovery, accounts) with QProcess on the GUI thread. On macOS Qt's vforkfd falls back to fork(), costing about 4 ms of main-thread time per launch in the large GUI process; Linux forks from the same thread.
acceptance_criteria: Launching and reaping hgs children no longer runs fork/exec on the GUI thread on macOS or Linux; timeouts, cancellation, ordering of results and error reporting stay unchanged; HgsClient tests pass.
notes: 2026-10-10: ProcessRunner owns all QProcess launches for runHgs, runWrite and requestRecovery on one worker thread (hgs-process-runner); results are queued to the owner on the GUI thread, owner destruction kills and reaps its children, a post routine reaps at exit; Linux uses UseVFork with Qt >= 6.7. GUI-thread cost per launch ~0.5 ms -> ~0.005 ms in a microbenchmark (the live profile showed ~4.2 ms fork). Residual on macOS: fork() takes malloc zone locks via atfork handlers, so a GUI allocation during a worker fork can still wait briefly; posix_spawn would avoid it. Branch perf/process-launch.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: full Qt suite passed on macOS (49/49) and Linux (48/48); in main as of b093ddb and installed on the Mac and arch on 2026-10-10.

title: Recovery jitter can exceed its 10% bound by a rounding error
description: recovery::schedule computed due_at as time + delay * (1.0 + jitter / 1000). For jitter 100, delay * 1.1 is not exact (90 * 1.1 = 99.00000000000001), so due_at exceeded the documented maximum and session_limits_wait_for_reset_and_interval_mode_uses_its_own_budget failed about once per 101 random job IDs (CI main for 6fd2598). Add the jitter separately.

title: Recovery keeps scheduling continuations while the agent is working
description: Observed with a Claude session on a rate-limited account: each recovery attempt goes dispatching -> retrying -> waiting within about 2 s because a new rate_limit provider hook arrives right after the continuation is delivered, while the agent stays busy/working and later answers (Claude appears to retry internally). Recovery reached attempt 11 and kept the panel at 'Waiting to retry (N attempts, repeats until stopped)' with the 'Limit reached' chip beside a working agent. Another Claude session on the same account received 11 queued '[HGS automatic recovery]' prompts in one user turn. Expected: a provider error followed by continued agent activity in the same turn must not schedule another continuation, the panel should not claim it is waiting to retry while the agent is working, and continuations must not queue up. Related: 2e28c15 reset-aware session limit recovery.
notes: Fix up as PR #56 (2026-10-14): accepted recovery episodes stay in progress while the agent keeps working; the account slot is released once the provider served the continuation (progress after the latest turn start). Root cause of the 11-attempt incidents was mostly a session limit read as rate limit, fixed earlier by 2e28c15.
close_reason: Merged in PR #56

design: Each explicitly connected gateway authorizes its own computer plus its enabled, directly configured Zerus peers. Bind each submitted request to its target and selected route, with no automatic rerouting of claimed or uncertain mutations. Keep credentials local, verify machine identity within dispatch, bound remote work, and invalidate dependent routes when an edge or gateway is removed. title: Make terminal scale validation portable across native font rounding

Diagnose font/grid behavior and correct the implementation or test fixture based on evidence before completing Mac deployment. Preserve published Arch assets and existing native sessions.
notes: Verified macOS counterexample: glyph advances 12.2969px and 24.6094px correctly double, but rounded cells are 13px and 25px, giving 51 and 27 columns in the unchanged viewport. The old half-column assertion is mathematically invalid under native font rounding. Runtime font scaling and grid metrics are correct. Replace that assertion with exact native-metric/viewport checks, retaining smaller grid, unchanged toolbar/context and full restore checks. Published Arch assets and runtime code remain unchanged.
close_reason: Native font diagnostics proved the runtime grid and scaling correct; replaced the invalid half-column assumption with exact font metrics and unchanged viewport checks. The complete terminal suite passes on Linux Qt 6.11 and Mac Qt 6.11; the other 33 Mac suites already passed. Runtime code and immutable release assets are unchanged.

title: Show every Claude tool approval in Activity
description: A Claude Read request outside the working directories showed only 'Needs input' in Activity; the native approval panel was visible only in Terminal. Two defects: (1) the permission_prompt Notification after PermissionRequest flips phase from approval to input; (2) Activity mirrors only Bash approvals. Level 1: keep the approval phase and always show a pending PermissionRequest card (tool + target) with an explicit Terminal fallback. Level 2: parse every Claude permission panel generically and expose its native options verbatim; persistent grants/blocks are marked and need an extra confirmation.
notes: Done in working tree: claude_approval.rs parses any Claude permission panel (title, body, question, numbered options, optional footer) and verifies it against the PermissionRequest (Bash command, file name, fetch host). Real PermissionRequest hooks carry no tool_use_id, so the previous Bash-only card never appeared outside the synthetic test. Options carry scope once/broader; the desktop asks for a second Confirm on broader ones. Unreadable/clipped/mismatched/plan panels show a Terminal-only card while a highlighted chooser is visible. PermissionRequest for AskUserQuestion now sets input; permission_prompt notifications no longer downgrade approval to input. Activity 'No' answers settle the session to interrupted. Follow-ups: zerus-h2u, zerus-9qq.

title: Escape closes Zerus instead of interrupting the working agent
description: b28c691 interrupts only when focus is inside Activity; anywhere else (session list, panel, no focus) Escape still calls close(). For Claude the Activity interrupt also never settles: after Escape Claude prints 'Interrupted · What should Claude do instead?' and emits no hook (verified with 2.1.294 against a fake API), so HGS keeps phase tool/working and the prompt is never restored. Escape must interrupt a working selected session from anywhere in the sessions page except Terminal, never close the window, and HGS must record a verified Claude interruption so the last prompt returns to the input.
notes: Done in working tree: SessionsWindow Escape no longer closes the window; it dismisses the peek, clears a focused search, then interrupts the selected working session from anywhere on the sessions page (Terminal and the message field handle their own Escape). interrupt.rs counts Claude's 'Interrupted · What should Claude do instead?' lines before Escape and, with the lock released, waits up to 3 s for one more; then it records the Interrupt (phase interrupted, tools cleared, journal event) and returns confirmed=true, so the GUI restores the last prompt. Tests: GUI escapeInterruptsFromAnywhereAndNeverCloses, test_session_actions Claude confirmation (fake PTY replies on Escape), native NativeClaudeInterrupt against Claude 2.1.294.

title: Persist unsent composer drafts across crashes and session termination
description: MessageComposer currently keeps text, attachments and delivery locks only in memory. Persist private per-machine/session and subagent drafts as edits happen, recover them after abrupt GUI termination, and keep unavailable or ended session drafts recoverable. Clear only confirmed outgoing payloads, preserve newer drafts and uncertain delivery locks, and do not automatically resend recovered input.
design: Persist every composer edit and cursor/selection change through a private atomic per-key manifest next to Qt settings. Snapshot attachment bytes independently and keep their hashes cached so typing never rewrites large files. Persist sending/uncertain states before transport; require explicit review after interrupted delivery. Keep a Saved drafts recovery dialog reachable without a live session. Persist question forms with exact run, conversation and question identity. GUI restarts on Linux and macOS are explicitly approved after the owner confirmed there is no unsent text. Exclude concurrently edited release version, workflow and packaging changes from this fix.

notes: Implemented private atomic drafts for text, cursor/selection, immutable attachment bytes and exact-identity question forms. Autosave occurs on edits; failed saves retry locally, and delivery starts only after recovery state is saved. Saved drafts stays accessible after session removal, with copy staying open and explicit replacement confirmation. Verified SIGKILL recovery after deleting the original attached file, failed/uncertain/confirmed delivery, per-machine/session/subagent isolation, rename conflicts and unchanged large attachment snapshots. Final merged GUIs are installed and managed by systemd/launchd. Original native/terminal process identities were preserved. Source checks passed; hosted CI was not dispatched.

title: Handle Codex question answers accepted into the native queue
description: An optional question answer entered the Codex native input queue while the agent was busy, but the adapter timed out waiting for the recorded reply and showed an uncertain-delivery error. design: Use a durable submitted status rather than inferring queue delivery from bounded native queue previews. Preserve exact run/conversation/question hash and canonical answers in the private question cache and receipt. Recover legacy in-progress composer attempts only from exact submitted input receipts. title: Add hgs guide and hgs self for agent coordination
description: Progressive-disclosure tier of the parent epic: an on-demand compact guide compiled into hgs and a verified self-identity command that the static hint and the sender envelope rely on.
design:
`hgs [@host] guide [topic]`: static text compiled into the binary. The base page (<= ~600 tokens, enforced by a byte-size test) covers identity (hgs self), ls/inspect, guarded send JSON shape and the never-resend-uncertain rule, how to reply, the wait protocol pointer, detached launch with --launch-id and ended_launches, and pause vs kill vs archive. Destructive operations (kill, stopping another owner's session) require explicit owner authorization; prefer pause. It also covers @host routing and the `hgs @host -h` capability probe. Topics: send, wait, launch, stop, remote. It routes over SSH like other read-only commands.

`hgs self --json`: resolve the caller through native process ancestry (session_graph::sends::send_origin), returning current name, machine UUID and route name, run_id, conversation_id and the same zerus:// reference `hgs reference` produces. After a rename it must find the binding by run identity instead of the stale HGS_SESSION. Unattributed callers (GUI/connector subprocesses, plain shells) get a clear nonzero error.
acceptance_criteria:
- guide base page and each topic stay under their byte budgets (tests); text is English and contains no paths or identifiers.
- `hgs @peer guide` returns the peer's guide; an older peer yields the normal unknown-command error.
- self returns the post-rename name, matches `hgs reference` output, and rejects callers without verified ancestry.
- docs/reference.md documents both commands.

title: Teach every Zerus-launched agent hgs coordination with minimal context
description: Owner request 2026-10-17: agents in any project, not only the zerus repository through its CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, must know that hgs lets them read, message, launch and stop other Zerus sessions on this and other computers. New sessions should pay the minimum context, and the knowledge must stay correct across resume, unpause, reboot restore, recovery, clear, compaction, fork and rename. Today Zerus injects nothing: agents get only HGS_* environment variables, and hgs send delivers bare text, so a recipient cannot tell another agent wrote it or how to reply.
design:
Progressive disclosure in three tiers, so a new session pays about 40 tokens once and the rest only when an agent actually coordinates.

1. Static hint, delivered to every agent hgs starts. One English sentence, at most ~50 tokens, byte-identical for every session and hgs version: no session name, ID, machine, version or path. Byte stability keeps prompt caches warm across resumes and upgrades and makes the hint rename-safe. Draft: "You are running in a Zerus session: the `hgs` CLI reads, messages, launches and stops other agent sessions on this and other computers; run `hgs guide` before using it."
2. `hgs [@host] guide [topic]`: a compact cheat sheet compiled into the binary (base page <= ~600 tokens; topics send, wait, launch, stop, remote for depth). It is version-matched by construction; `@host` returns that peer's own guide, and the guide tells agents to probe `hgs @host -h` before using commands an older peer may lack. docs/ remains the specification; the guide links to it rather than restating it.
3. `hgs self --json`: the caller's current session name, machine, run and conversation and its copyable zerus:// reference, proven through native process ancestry (reuse session_graph::sends::send_origin). HGS_SESSION is fixed at launch, so this command must resolve the current name after a rename.

Hint delivery chooses, per provider, a native channel that never replaces user instructions and never accumulates in history:
- hgs-owned engines (official DeepSeek Harness, OpenCode native API): add the hint to the instructions hgs already builds.
- Claude Code, Codex, Kimi: preferred channel is the SessionStart hook hgs already installs, returning additional context only for a verified tracked run (works for project launchers too). Emit on startup, clear and compact. On resume, emit only when the binding has no delivery mark for that exact conversation, so pre-feature conversations learn on their next resume and repeated resumes add nothing. Fallback where a hook cannot add context: a launch-time instruction flag merged with any user-supplied value (Claude --append-system-prompt, Codex developer instructions), added on every launch and resume but never saved in the run's base argv. This is the existing statusline pattern in src/state/lifecycle.rs ("The saved base stays as launched; resume adds the settings again").
- Verify each mechanism against the pinned native versions before adoption; when none is verified, skip with a diagnostic instead of guessing.
- Never teach a live agent by sending it a message, never edit user-owned CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, and do not target arbitrary commands (hgs sh) or native subagents.

Receiving side: an agent-originated hgs send (attribution already proven by send_origin) wraps its text in one compact envelope carrying the sender's name, machine and zerus:// reference, which is enough for `hgs inspect` and a reply. Owner, desktop and phone sends stay bare. Activity renders the envelope as a peer message (journal::system_prompt already classifies Claude's own cross-session envelopes as peer_message).

Controls: on by default; opt-out in hgs configuration globally and per account. `hgs guide` and `hgs self` always work.

Docs: new reference.md section and agent-coordination.md update; afterwards trim the repository CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md guidance that the hint and guide make redundant (mirror both files).
acceptance_criteria:
- A new agent of every supported provider learns about hgs coordination at a fixed cost of <= ~50 tokens, with no repository instructions.
- Lifecycle matrix verified, each with exactly one hint in effective context: new launch (CLI, desktop, Android, iOS, detached --launch-id), resume/unpause, resume --all after reboot, automatic recovery, archive restore, resume --fresh and live Clear session, native and hgs compaction, fork, rename (hint unchanged, hgs self returns the new name), hgs upgrade between launch and resume, remote launch through a peer.
- Older peers inject nothing and fail no launch; mixed-version guidance is in the guide.
- User instruction flags, project launchers and saved base argv are preserved; opt-out works.
- Recipients of agent-originated sends can identify the sender and reply without other context.

comments.author: ufna
comments.text:
Timing diagnosis for the #157 failure (run 38821503313, CLI ubuntu-24.04, `test_new_conversation_discards_old_pending_intent` at line 245):

- **Sender:** `hgs send` (`src/state/input.rs` `submit`) pastes the text, sleeps 180 ms, sends Enter as a separate `terminal.send(pane, Enter)` (tmux send-keys writes `\r` into the pane's pty), marks the receipt `submitted` and returns. It never waits for the agent to read that `\r`, and by design it never retries Enter.
- **Enter was sent:** a failed Enter returns `delivery uncertain` with a non-zero exit. The test's `returncode == 0` assertion on line 244 passed, so tmux accepted the Enter.
- **Recorder:** the fixture agent (`tests/test_input.py` `FAKE_AGENT`) is a separate process that `select`s on the pty and appends each `read()` chunk to `received`. Because of the 180 ms gap, the paste and the `\r` arrive as separate reads. The `\r` reaches the file only after the fixture process is scheduled again, which can be after `hgs send` has exited.
- **Observed:** `received` held the full bracketed paste (written 180 ms or more before Enter) and lacked only the trailing `\r`. That matches this window exactly. A transport fault would show a missing or partial paste, or a non-zero exit.
- **#157's source:** its only `input.rs` change is a synchronous `claude_usage_limit::current` guard in `checked_input`, before the paste. It does not touch the paste→Enter path or anything after it.
- **Precedent:** the same race was fixed for the busy send test in #143 (zerus-kpl4). This PR applies the same wait to the remaining two tests that compare `received` right after `hgs send`.

title: Commit ancestry does not answer whether useful changes were already integrated
description:
A synthetic worktree with identical final Git tree to main after a squash-style integration is Review, merged=false, ahead=1. Current merge state checks ancestor reachability only. Pushed checks local tracking refs without fetching; the overview omits these facts. Unknown and stale evidence require distinct presentation.
Proposed direction: Distinguish ancestry, equivalent changes and verified remaining differences. Show a named base and ref freshness. Patch/tree equivalence can help explain cherry-pick/squash results but must not alone authorize branch deletion; keep branch retention and guarded git branch -d.

title: Windows: Ctrl+C and other control keys do not reach Codex 0.162 through the session host
description: Found by the real-agent Windows suite (tests/test_windows_native_agents.py, NativeWindowsCodex.test_input_keys_reach_codex_through_the_host; the spike S2 checks folded in from zerus-ziq3.7.13) on the Windows test PC, Codex 0.162.0 win32, bundled ConPTY, twice. Sent through hgs __host backend op send: a lone Esc then literal text arrives whole ('esc probe' shows in the composer), but a single Ctrl+C (C-c, 0x03) leaves the draft in place for 120 s, and C-e C-u do not clear it either. The record stays activity unknown with no error. The same keys work for Claude Code 2.1.296 through the same host path: Ctrl+C clears its draft, C-e C-u clear it, and text typed after Ctrl+S shows. Spike S2 saw Codex not clear on raw ConPTY too. S2 measured Codex's console input mode as 0x0098 (no ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_INPUT, no ENABLE_PROCESSED_INPUT), so crossterm reads INPUT_RECORDs, and how ConPTY turns C0 bytes into key events (virtual key and LEFT_CTRL_PRESSED) decides whether Codex sees Ctrl+letter. Determine what Codex receives and fix the host's key encoding for agents without VT input (for example, write KEY_EVENTs with the control state for named C-x keys) so that Ctrl+C clears or interrupts Codex as in a real console. Blocks closing zerus-ziq3.7.13 and gating windows-host.
notes:
Hypothesis (2026-10-14, host side): Codex's console input mode 0x0098 (S2) has neither ENABLE_PROCESSED_INPUT nor ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_INPUT, so it reads INPUT_RECORDs and ConPTY turns a raw C0 byte (0x03, 0x15) written by the host into a key event without LEFT_CTRL_PRESSED, which crossterm does not read as Ctrl+letter. Both ConPTY builds ask the terminal for win32-input-mode (DECSET 9001, S1); the host strips it (src/host/sequences.rs) and writes plain VT input. Candidate fix: encode Ctrl+letter (from named keys and from attach clients' C0 bytes) as win32-input-mode sequences CSI Vk;Sc;Uc;Kd;Cs;Rc _ with the Ctrl state, as Windows Terminal does once 9001 is requested; ConPTY turns them back into VT for apps that read VT input (Claude, Kimi). Probe with real Codex and Claude (raw vs win32 C-c and C-u) prepared for the Windows PC.
Root cause confirmed 2026-10-14 by probe on the Windows PC (real Codex 0.162.0 and Claude Code 2.1.296 through the host, bundled ConPTY): crossterm on Windows (src/event/sys/windows/parse.rs) resolves a key event whose u_char is a control character (< 0x20) with ToUnicodeEx in the keyboard layout of the foreground window; the PC's active layout is Russian, so Ctrl+C reaches Codex as Ctrl+'с' (Cyrillic) and Codex ignores it. Raw 0x03 and win32-input-mode with Uc=3 both fail; win32-input-mode with no Ctrl typed 'с'. A win32-input-mode key with the Latin letter as Uc (CSI 67;46;99;1;8;1_ then ...;0;8;1_) clears Codex's composer for Ctrl+C and Ctrl+U, and Claude (VT input) still clears with every form. Hosted CI runners with a US layout may not show the bug. Fix: the host encodes Ctrl+letter (named keys and attach clients' C0 bytes, outside escape sequences and bracketed paste) as win32-input-mode keys with the Latin letter and LEFT_CTRL_PRESSED while the console has requested DECSET 9001.
Fix up as PR #54 (2026-10-14, branch p2/win32-ctrl-keys): while the console has requested DECSET 9001, the host sends a lone Ctrl+letter (0x01-0x1A except BS/TAB/LF/CR), from backend key sends and from attach clients' typed input, as win32-input-mode key-down/up records with the Latin letter and LEFT_CTRL_PRESSED; pastes, escape sequences and query replies stay raw. Verified on the Windows PC: named C-c and C-u clear the draft in real Codex 0.162.0 and Claude 2.1.296.
PR #54 first version regressed VT-input consoles in hosted CI (fake agent got 'c' for C-c; ConPTY turns a win32 key record into its Uc for a console with ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_INPUT; real Claude passed only because libuv reads key records). Rework: convert hgs's own key sends only when the supervisor reports the agent's console input mode without VT input (Codex 0x0098); attach typing stays raw, as any native terminal sends it (Codex under a non-Latin layout then behaves as in Windows Terminal, an upstream crossterm limitation). Product path: input_queue.rs sends C-s for 'ctrl-s to steer immediately'.
close_reason: Merged in PR #54: Ctrl+letter key sends reach a key-record console (Codex) as win32-input-mode records with the Latin letter; verified on the Windows PC with real Codex and Claude and the real-agent suite (6/6 each)

title: Windows: hgs answer leaves a Codex async question reply unsubmitted in the composer
description: Found by the real-agent Windows suite (tests/test_windows_native_agents.py, NativeWindowsCodex.test_hgs_answers_request_user_input_async; zerus-ziq3.7.12) on the Windows test PC, twice, with Codex 0.162.0 win32 through the session host (bundled ConPTY). Codex calls request_user_input_async from the fake API and its turn ends, so the panel is gone and codex_questions::answer takes the input::submit path with the <send_user_message_question_reply> envelope (multi-line JSON). hgs answer returns status 'submitted' (the 6 s confirmation wait expires). The captured screen 120 s later still shows the whole envelope in Codex's composer, the fake API never receives a fourth request, and the record keeps input_pending_at. So the paste arrived but its Enter did not submit. On Linux the same case passes. Plain hgs send messages, including a short multiline one, submit fine through the host, so suspect the longer multi-line paste: Enter 180 ms after it (spike S2 criterion d) may still fall inside Codex's Windows paste-burst handling, or ConPTY may deliver the paste in pieces. Reproduce with the suite on Windows; check what Codex receives (bracketed paste vs key events) and whether hgs should wait for a settled composer before Enter or resend Enter after verifying the draft.
notes: Root cause (2026-10-14, from Codex tui/src/bottom_pane/paste_burst.rs): chars <=8 ms apart form a paste burst (60 ms idle timeout on Windows) and an Enter within PASTE_ENTER_SUPPRESS_WINDOW = 120 ms of the last burst char inserts a newline. Codex on Windows reads console key events (no VT input, mode 0x0098 in S2), so ConPTY delivers hgs's bracketed paste as typed keys; the 210-byte reply is still being processed when hgs's Enter arrives at its fixed 180 ms. Candidate fix on branch p2/codex-paste-enter (4a8da2d): for Codex on Windows, poll the plain capture until the composer shows the whole paste (or Codex's [Pasted Content placeholder), within 2 s + 4 ms/byte, then 200 ms, then the single Enter; Unix keeps 180 ms. Verification requested from the native-suite session on the Windows PC.
close_reason: Merged in PR #48 (verified with the real-agent Windows suite)

title: durableSubmissionKeepsGuiResponsive(send-expiry) hung a Windows sessionswindow shard
description: Trusted main run 38523322814 at be17b70 (Windows client, desktop and portable zip, job 115719062635): CTest killed sessionswindow-0 after 240 s. The shard's output ends at QWARN for TestSessionsWindow::durableSubmissionKeepsGuiResponsive(send-expiry) with no PASS/FAIL, so the process hung without a QTRY timeout firing, which suggests the GUI thread was blocked. The test holds the draft store's first write on a semaphore (ComposerDraftStore::setWriteObserver: entered.release(); release.acquire()) and only releases it after the warm-cache expiry deadline passes (QTRY_VERIFY on currentSecsSinceEpoch() >= expires_at). Hypothesis to check first: some path the GUI thread takes while the write is held (expiry handling, a re-render or draft save) waits synchronously for the writer (flushWrites or similar), so the test's own block deadlocks the GUI. If so, determine whether a real slow disk could do the same to the product (GUI blocked until a write completes) or whether only the test's indefinite block can. The rows did not change in PR #44; the failed jobs were re-run to see whether it repeats.
notes: Cause confirmed: the expiry rows set a warm cache until now + 2 whole seconds; if the cache expired before the click (slow details.json replacement on Windows), admission opened the modal coldCacheConfirm / questionColdCacheConfirm and nothing answered it. A 2.1 s QTest::qSleep before the click hangs the unpatched row deterministically on Linux (rc 124, no output, like CI). Not a product deadlock: the draft store's observer runs outside its mutex and no GUI path calls the blocking store helpers. Fix in PR #47: now + 4, a 10 s expiry wait, and a zero-timer guard that rejects either confirmation and fails the row with a message.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #47 (e241318), test only. The expiry rows gave the warm cache as little as 1 s before the click; an expired cache at admission opened the modal cold-cache confirmation that nothing answered, hanging the shard. Now now + 4 (at least 3 s), a 10 s expiry wait, and a zero-timer guard that rejects either confirmation and fails with a message. Injected 2.1 s delay: unpatched hangs (rc 124, as on CI), patched passes; 4.1 s: patched fails fast. Windows test PC: patched 96/96 send-expiry, 48/48 question-expiry, 16/16 all rows, no hangs; PR CI run 38526727144 green.

title: hgs terminate on Windows refuses while the host still lists the ended session
description: Found by the terminal backend contract against the session host (PR #41, hosted Windows CI run 38511780818, job 115681739103): test_terminate_waits_for_the_agent_then_archives_the_session got 'hgs: session is still running; its saved binding was kept'. Not reproduced in 4 runs on the Windows test PC, so it is timing dependent. Path (src/state/terminate.rs): after kill_session, terminate waits only for the agent process to exit, then takes the state lock and checks live(). On the host the session stays listed until its --run supervisor has run supervisor::finish (which needs that same state lock), exited and been drained by the host (registry::ended), so live() can still contain the name. On tmux kill-session removes it at once. Expected (contract): 'hgs: terminated and archived NAME (...)', the agent ended by the close signals, the session archived. Candidate fix: on the host, wait (bounded by the existing deadline) until the backend no longer lists the session before taking the lock and checking live(), so the supervisor can finish; keep the safety checks and the 'archived' path if the supervisor archived first. The same window may affect kill and pause listing (contract review).
notes: Fix up as PR #43 (2026-10-14): on Windows terminate waits, without the state lock and within its 20 s deadline, until the host no longer lists the terminated run, so the supervisor can record the exit and end; Unix makes no extra tmux call. Pause already waits unlocked; kill does not check the listing afterwards.
close_reason: Fixed by the Phase 2 owner session in PR #43 (043a3b4): Windows terminate waits for the listing without holding the lock. Verified by the host backend contract suite (PR #41, merged 88cdd3f): test_terminate_waits_for_the_agent_then_archives_the_session and the other 11 cases passed 4/4 rounds on the Windows test PC and in hosted Windows CI run 38514919925.

title: Qualify coldCacheConfirmationPreservesDraftAndPinsConversation on Windows
description: PR #40 Windows CI run 38506309544 (job 115664554827), a packaging change that does not touch the desktop, failed TestSessionsWindow::coldCacheConfirmationPreservesDraftAndPinsConversation: 'shown' returned FALSE at tray/tests/test_sessionswindow.cpp(1774). The macOS crash of the same test (zerus-c9p) was fixed and closed; this is the Windows form. Reproduce with loaded parallel runs on the Windows PC (as for zerus-0jix/a0ak, 48 parallel processes) and fix with an exact barrier without weakening the draft and conversation-pin assertions.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #44 (be17b70), test only. Cause: on Windows, Qt 6.10 runs a coarse timer of 20 ms or less as a multimedia timer that posts its QTimerEvent (qeventdispatcher_win.cpp), so the test's 5 ms confirmation timer shared a sendPostedEvents() batch with queued ProcessRunner replies. The reply of the window's show-time inspection, which had read the old conversation, could be delivered after the accept and before exec() returned. It restored conversation-cache, the second confirmation started a send, and the third click found a disabled button ('shown' FALSE at 1774). The product stays safe: the payload pins expected_conversation_id. Fix: setDetailsPollForTests(500, 24 h); wait (15 s) for the reply to the test's own inspection, and for the reply to the inspection started by the conversation change; assert !isSending after each refused confirmation. Reproduced on Linux with timing injection (original 16/16 fail, fixed 24/24 + 120/120 under load). Windows test PC: unpatched 96/96 (not reproduced there), fixed 96/96 including a round on a freshly built binary; hosted CI run 38521674575 green.

description: CI38417870500 at61e1d21 passes the original three recovery cases, desktop matrices and Linux CLI but macOS CLI speech peer submit reports Socket is not connected (os error57). No live services or native agents may be restarted.
notes:
Exact frozen macOS speech peer contract passed 25 consecutive isolated repetitions. Hosted failure remains intermittent; retain the socket half-close diagnostic rather than treating it as a regression in conversation history. Retry failed jobs on the same sealed source/CI build identity; do not rebuild or replace published bytes.
Deterministic actual Mac UnixStream-pair probe: server reads the complete newline request, writes schema1 response, closes and joins before client half-close. shutdown(Write) then returns code57/NotConnected, while read_to_string still returns the intact valid response. This confirms a real fast-close portability defect; narrow production repair and closed-peer response validation qualification are now required.
Qualified final source handles only NotConnected from write-half-close and still requires the original bounded JSON/schema read. Three focused tests cover real peer-close before half-close, strict invalid/empty/oversized/wrong-schema responses, and preservation of other shutdown/read failures. title: Decide how the desktop opens executable attachments
description: Attachment chips and Activity attachments open cached copies with QDesktopServices::openUrl, i.e. the platform default handler. Files written by Zerus carry no download origin marker, so an attachment received from a remote conversation with an executable or shell-handled type (for example .exe, .bat, .cmd, .ps1, .url, .scf on Windows; .command or .app bundles on macOS; .desktop on Linux) is handed to the system with no additional prompt. zerus-fn6d removed only the .lnk case, because Qt also mis-validated it. Decide the product behaviour, for example: reveal in the file manager instead of opening, require a confirmation that names the type, or mark the cached copy with the platform's downloaded-file origin. Then apply it to AttachmentLoader::open and MessageComposer::openAttachment consistently, with tests per platform.
close_reason: Owner chose browser-like opening. Files from other machines carry the platform downloaded-file marker (Windows Mark of the Web, macOS quarantine); anything that would run a program is selected in the file manager instead of opened, on every platform (tray/src/ExternalFile). Covers Activity attachments, draft attachments, downloads and file references. Verified locally and on Windows; reviewed in three rounds.

title: Quit the desktop GUI gracefully on SIGTERM and own its live update in the repository
description: hgs-tray has no SIGTERM handler, so systemctl restart/stop and launchctl unload in tray/install.sh kill it before aboutToQuit runs DraftWrites::flush; queued draft writes can be lost. Agents therefore wrote ad-hoc /tmp update scripts (tray menu Quit, staging in ~/Applications or ~/.local/bin, verification) and left .zerus-* staging folders and old bundles behind. (1) Handle SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP on Unix by calling the same quit as the tray menu; a repeated signal keeps its default action. (2) Provide one repository-owned live update for the installed GUI: unique staging beside the target removed on every outcome, graceful quit (SIGTERM when the running build supports it, otherwise the platform quit request), exactly one rollback copy in a fixed location, restart through the service manager, verification that nonempty drafts and native agent/tmux process identities are unchanged, and ~/.local/share/hgs/build-provenance.json. tray/install.sh uses it when replacing a running GUI. Follow-ups: one-time sweep of legacy .zerus-* folders and an agent protocol rule.
close_reason: Done in ea3d52d: SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP quit through the tray's Quit; tray/install.sh replaces a changed GUI via tray/update-installed.py (unique staging, graceful quit, one rollback copy, restart, draft/native/image checks, build-provenance.json). Verified live on Linux 2026-10-12: a running pre-handler GUI quit through its tray menu, 70 nonempty drafts and 17 native processes kept; the new GUI's SigCgt includes SIGTERM. macOS process/socket/image detection verified read-only.

This is avoidable steady work, not independently proven to cause the reported full freeze.

title: Desktop reply banners fire for Kimi scheduled cron ticks and lost focus/idle gating
description: On macOS, each routine reply from a Kimi recurring cron job (CronCreate */15) posts a 'Zerus — New reply' banner. Two causes, verified 2026-10-11: (1) the zerus-vww8 idle gating and zerus-w9sm application-focus suppression were only hot-patched into installed GUI binaries and never committed; installing main 3901833 (0.41.0) on Linux and macOS removed them (installed binaries no longer import QGuiApplication::applicationState). (2) Even with idle gating, a cron-fired Kimi turn ends fully idle (activity/phase idle, no children), so every scheduled tick is a banner-eligible reply. Kimi 2.1.1 sends originKind=cron_job/cron_missed in its TurnStarted hook and journals cron.add/cron.delete in wire.jsonl; hgs drops both. Expected: re-land focus suppression and idle gating; scheduled-tick replies stay unread but do not banner while the scheduled job remains, and the final reply after the job is removed still notifies.
notes:
Follow-up 2026-10-11: owner reported the 21:30 tick still 'notified'. Notification Center showed no Zerus banner after the 21:24 Mac deploy; the remaining signal was the unread mark/badge, which the first fix intentionally kept. Now hgs does not advance reply_id for scheduled ticks while recurring_schedules > 0, and a read reply never moves back behind the read mark during skipping (transition from pre-origin journal rows).
Original implementation (55bc4e4): hgs journals Kimi TurnStarted origin_kind as turn_origin; Kimi sessions report recurring_schedules folded from wire.jsonl cron.add/cron.delete (one-shot excluded; null while unknown); AttentionTracker re-lands zerus-w9sm focus suppression and zerus-vww8 idle gating and consumes scheduled replies silently while recurring jobs remain. Validation: Rust unit tests, scripts/ci/cli.sh (63 modules, 0 failed), all 52 Qt CTest suites, installed on Linux and macOS with native identities and drafts unchanged; 21:30 tick verified reply_scheduled=true without a Notification Center banner.
close_reason: Fixed in 55bc4e4 and d8ceeab; installed on Linux and macOS. Live: the 21:30 tick reported reply_scheduled without a Notification Center banner, and after d8ceeab the 21:45 tick left reply_id on the read reply (no unread mark, badge or banner).

title: test_late_dispatch_target_cleans_after_gateway_deadline: late target process survived on Ubuntu CI
description: test_mobile_worktrees_transport.WorktreeTransport.test_late_dispatch_target_cleans_after_gateway_deadline failed once on CI (ubuntu-24.04) in run 38122605296 (b634f8a, which only changed test timing elsewhere): 'late target Git/native process survived its own mobile budget' at tests/test_mobile_worktrees_transport.py:43 after the 9 s wait; the message does not say whether the post-checkout hook or the late remote native hgs survived. First failure in the last 40 main CI runs; CLI (macos-15) passed in the same run. Determine whether the mobile budget cleanup is unreliable or the test margin is too tight.
notes: 2026-10-11 root cause: test helper, not the connector. The CI test lasted 35.2 s, so the wait loop ended early when both processes looked dead (zombies, ~t35) and the immediate re-check in assertFalse saw one as alive. Linux briefly reports state X (dead) while a parent reaps a zombie; MobilePeers.running() treated anything but Z as running. Probe on Arch (5000 reaps): Z->X->gone in 479 cases, 477 dead-then-alive flips with the old rule, 0 when X counts as dead. Locally the mobile budget kills the hook and late native hgs at ~t36 against a t39 window (24/24 loaded runs). Fix: treat X like Z in running() and the four other test zombie checks (test_process_control single-shot check, test_input/test_pause/test_mobile_worktrees_native wait loops).
close_reason: Fixed in 5eed3d3: process-state test checks treat X (dead) like Z; CLI (ubuntu-24.04) and CLI (macos-15) passed in run 38124360082, which includes it.

title: Show repository publication status on session cards
description:
## Summary
The owner wants the session card to show whether work has been pushed because local-only work has nearly been lost. Design a compact repository/branch publication indicator beside the existing project/branch line, distinguishing tracked and untracked working changes, commits ahead of the tracked remote, absent upstream and stale or unavailable remote verification. Status belongs to the actual session folder and branch and can be shared by several sessions; do not imply feature ownership or completed remote backup from a stale local ref.

## Acceptance Criteria
A reviewable design shows local changes and unpublished commits separately, with repository identity, remote/upstream and last verification in details. Synced requires adequate current evidence. Non-Git folders, worktrees, detached HEAD, divergent branches and offline machines have explicit states. No automatic commit, push, discard or cleanup. Implement after the product design is agreed.
design: The owner approved the trial on 2026-10-10. Implemented native outline diff, upload, download and cloud check/question icons beside the project/branch line. Distinct counters preserve local file changes and outgoing/incoming commits, with conflict color and exact hover details. Publication verification is read-only and separate from fleet/agent polling; local tracking refs alone never imply a verified remote. Worktrees use their own checkout identity; archives and ordinary non-Git folders have no live publication badge. See docs/reference.md for evidence, refresh, expiration and compatibility behavior.
notes:
Implemented and validated locally without committing or publishing this trial. Rust 1.85: 196 unit tests passed. Ten isolated real-Git publication contracts and 16 existing worktree contracts passed. Qt client/workspace suites passed (74 and 16 cases); integrated session-card checks passed, including shared-folder deduplication, unchanged draft/selection/focus, both themes and 280/360/500 px layouts. Desktop builds and source/privacy checks passed. Native Qt previews are in /tmp/zerus-git-status-preview.
Owner explicitly authorized commit and push on 2026-10-10. Publication is scoped to Git status badges and their read-only backend; other active work is excluded.
Owner-authorized publication completed on 2026-10-10: commit a753770 is pushed to origin/main after rebasing onto concurrent reviewed main updates. The exact integrated revision builds the desktop and passes 198 Rust 1.85 unit tests, 10 isolated Git publication contracts, all 23 worktree contracts, Qt client/workspace suites (74/16 passes including setup and cleanup), and focused integrated window checks (6 passes). Source/privacy gates pass; drafts, selection and editor focus are preserved.

title: Separate session-limit recovery with reset-time and interval policies
description:
## Summary
A confirmed Claude session limit with a reset time currently enters the temporary rate-limit retry schedule. Add a distinct session_limit class with a default wait-for-reset policy and an optional per-class delay sequence using existing recovery syntax. Parse native reset evidence with its event time and timezone, preserve manual handling of permanent quota/billing/authentication failures, and expose settings and waiting status.

## Acceptance Criteria
Existing policies migrate without losing schedules. Session-limit recovery defaults to the known reset deadline, supports interval retries, and safely handles missing reset evidence. Tests cover native classification/reset extraction, policy compatibility, cancellation, class switching and settings round trips. Update reference documentation.
notes:
Implemented session_limit recovery policy v3 with default reset mode and optional independent interval schedule (300,0 fallback), native error/reset normalization, legacy episode migration, shared Qt settings and reset status. Verified 195 Rust tests on Rust 1.85, 13 isolated recovery integration tests, focused Qt recovery/settings/quota regressions (9 passes including setup/cleanup), source/privacy checks and dependency notice collection. Qt qualification used a temporary HEAD tray checkout with only this feature overlaid because existing in-progress zerus-6i4u changes have undefined Start fresh methods in the working tree. No commit, deployment or remote sync.

The exact staged source tree builds hgs-tray and passes 193 Rust tests on Rust 1.85, 13 private recovery integration tests and the focused Qt recovery/settings/quota suite (9 passes including setup/cleanup), plus source/privacy checks. The lower Rust count excludes the separate in-progress Start fresh work. Unrelated working changes remain local. Repository publication indicators are tracked separately in zerus-l8v7.
