title: Remove global relay maintenance from polling hot paths and bound poll concurrency
description: Performance audit 2026-10-09. server.py:273-282 invokes Store.maintain on every 250 ms node poll; receipt reads and submissions also run it. store.py:143-159 scans terminal request history and events, heartbeat():261-263 scans global capped tables, and SQLite/fsync run on the HTTP event loop. A synthetic one-second empty long poll executed 81 SQL statements including 45 UPDATE/DELETE statements. With 100000 mutation tombstones and 100000 small events, median maintenance was 43.5 ms and heartbeat cleanup 34.4 ms on the audit workstation. An unrelated 0.5 s SQLite writer lock stalled a simultaneous health request for 0.53 s. Move bounded indexed retention work to an independent cadence and serialized DB worker, preserve just-in-time claim expiry, and cap active long polls per credential/workspace.
acceptance_criteria: Measure event-loop latency and work per idle connector at growing history sizes; cancelled/disconnected polls release capacity, simultaneous polls are bounded, health remains responsive during DB waits, and command claims retain crash/no-replay guarantees.
close_reason: Implemented and independently reviewed in the uncommitted relay candidate: trusted proxy identity and isolated admission, bounded warm payload handling, transactional result reservations/retention accounting, async PostgreSQL multiworker storage with notification waits and bounded background maintenance. Integrated203 service tests and20 final-image256MiB cgroup cases pass. Production cutover remains a separate operation.

title: Research anonymous Android dev distribution and update delivery
description: Compare primary-source options for public APK downloads without tester registration, publishing APIs and in-app update checks. Assess Android installation constraints, signing continuity, current developer verification rollout, and recommend a Zerus dev distribution architecture. Research only; no runtime implementation or deployment.
notes: Research completed 2026-10-09 from primary sources. Recommendation (not yet an implementation decision): public static HTTPS channel manifest plus immutable signed APKs on existing hosting; GitHub prereleases as archive/mirror; optional Obtainium deep link. No user authentication for metadata/downloads, publisher credentials kept private. Native Android PackageInstaller supports conditional self-updates without user action on Android 12+, with install-source approval, current target API and UPDATE_PACKAGES_WITHOUT_USER_ACTION; always handle STATUS_PENDING_USER_ACTION. GitHub releases/latest excludes prereleases and public REST calls are limited to 60/hour per originating IP; Actions artifacts require sign-in. Obtainium and own F-Droid binary repos offer account-free client-managed updates. Appcircle public testing links support auth=None; its in-app update API is a separate Enterprise App Store feature. Diawi expiration/installation limits suit temporary handoffs. Expo EAS internal URLs permit anonymous access by default. Firebase requires tester Google sign-in; App Center distribution is retired. Current Google FAQ explicitly exempts direct sideloading from the September 2026 initial participating-store rollout; prepare for the announced 2027 expansion. Local source: pilot is nondebuggable but still uses debug signingConfig, no updater/installer permissions implemented. Public APK HEAD was HTTP 200 without credentials. Signing continuity and existing installed data must be preserved before broad distribution. Sources: https://developer.android.com/reference/android/content/pm/PackageInstaller.SessionParams ; https://developer.android.com/developer-verification/guides/faq ; https://docs.github.com/en/rest/releases/releases ; https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api ; https://wiki.obtainium.imranr.dev/app_tracking/ ; https://f-droid.org/en/docs/Setup_an_F-Droid_App_Repo/ ; https://docs.appcircle.io/testing-distribution/create-or-select-a-distribution-profile ; https://docs.appcircle.io/enterprise-app-store/in-app-updates ; https://www.diawi.com/features-services ; https://docs.expo.dev/build/internal-distribution/ ; https://firebase.google.com/docs/app-distribution/get-set-up-as-a-tester?platform=android ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/appcenter/distribution/uploading . No runtime or deployment changes made for this research.
close_reason: Primary-source comparison and project-specific recommendation completed; no implementation requested.

title: Claude task notifications appear as user messages in Activity
description: When a background command finishes, Claude Code starts a new turn whose prompt is a raw <task-notification> XML envelope and fires UserPromptSubmit with it (verified with Claude 2.1.294 against a local fake API; the hook input has no origin field, while the transcript marks promptSource=system, origin.kind=task-notification). HGS journals it as UserPromptSubmit, so Activity renders it as 'You ... Sent' with literal tags, and the session prompt is overwritten. Keep the turn lifecycle, but journal and render it as a system notice with the summary, and do not replace the user's last prompt. Already journaled rows should render correctly too.
notes: Done in working tree: journal::task_notification parses Claude's <task-notification> envelope(s); log_event and journal reads mark such UserPromptSubmit/Queued/TurnStarted rows with origin=task_notification, task_status and the summary as detail (legacy rows too). The turn lifecycle is unchanged, but record.prompt is not overwritten and user_prompt() hides legacy notification prompts from summaries/inspect/search. Search maps notices to role event and skips Claude transcript user turns with origin.kind=task-notification. Activity renders a violet 'Background task' card (dark #c5a8f5/#2a2536, light #6c43b8/#f4f0fb).

title: Claude subagent hand-backs appear as user messages in Activity
description: When a background subagent finishes, Claude Code queues its final report as a prompt '<agent-message from="<agent id>">[Subagent hand-back] ...' (transcript attachment queued_command, origin.kind=peer, handback=true, isMeta=true) and fires UserPromptSubmit with it. HGS journals it as the person's message, so Activity shows 'You ... Sent' with the raw envelope. Extend the task notification handling (zerus-9rz) to agent-message envelopes: keep the turn lifecycle, show a subagent report notice instead of You, render the report as agent Markdown, and keep it out of the session prompt and user-role search.
notes: Done in working tree: journal::system_prompt parses <task-notification> and <agent-message from=...> envelopes (hand-back frame stripped, 2-space report indentation removed). mark_system_prompt sets origin=subagent_report, detail 'Agent "<description>" finished' (description captured at SubagentStart from the single unclaimed active Agent/Task call), report (<=32000 chars) and from_agent. Activity shows a violet 'Subagent report' with one line and a '▸ Show report' toggle rendering the Markdown. Legacy rows fall back to the report's first line; their report is limited to the 1200-character journal excerpt.

title: Show agent thinking as a quiet, always-expanded card
description: Thinking currently renders as a collapsed operational group: a small muted 'Thinking' title and a clipped preview line. Render it like an agent reply instead (full text, same size and Markdown) but quieter: no card fill, a thin pale left bar, muted text and a 'Thinking' label.
notes: Done in working tree: ActivityView renders AgentThinking as a full card (no toggle) with the page background instead of a card fill, a pale bar (#4f6680/#aec3dc), a readable muted label (#8ea3bd/#4f6b8f) and Markdown at full size with dimmer text (#b9c2cd/#424a53).

title: Escape in Activity interrupts the turn and restores its prompt
description: In Activity, Escape behaves like in Terminal: it interrupts a working turn (same verified interrupt as Stop). When the turn ends up interrupted, the prompt of that turn returns to the empty Activity composer so it can be edited and resent. Drafts are never overwritten; clipped or automatic-recovery prompts are not restored.

title: Show Claude's suggested next message as the composer placeholder
description: Claude's next-message suggestion arrives as a SubagentStop of an internal agent (no SubagentStart, no agent type) seconds after the turn ends. Activity showed it as 'Subagent finished'. Keep it as the session's prompt_suggestion instead, show it as the empty composer's placeholder, insert it with Tab, and clear it on a new prompt, turn, conversation or send.

title: Mark sessions with an unsent draft by a Draft status
description: When a session's composer holds text or attachments, the agent is not working and asks nothing, its row shows a quiet Draft status (pencil badge). Priority: Attention/Error > Working > Draft > New reply > Paused > Ready; unread stays as the extra badge. Not shown for the session open in the panel.

title: Claude cross-session messages appear as user messages in Activity
description: A message from another local Claude session reaches the agent as a '<cross-session-message from="uds:..." from-name="<session>" from-mode="...">' prompt and fires UserPromptSubmit (transcript: promptSource=system, origin.kind=peer, isMeta). Activity shows it as 'You ... Sent' with raw tags. Show it as a violet 'Message from <session>' notice with the full text, and keep it out of the session prompt and user-role search.

title: Run the test suites in parallel
description: Python integration modules run strictly one after another (~286 s on a 32-core machine, test_pause alone 80 s) and ctest runs Qt suites with --parallel 1 (~157 s, sessionswindow 92 s). Run Python test classes as parallel jobs (ZERUS_TEST_JOBS, default min(cores, 8)) with per-module logs and the same summary, run ctest in parallel with isolated per-test HOME/config, and split test_sessionswindow into function shards.
notes: Done in working tree: scripts/ci/python-tests.py runs TestCase classes (larger ones split into jobs of at most 12 tests unless they define setUpClass) in parallel fresh processes, slowest first from artifacts/test-results/python/durations.json; ZERUS_TEST_JOBS, default min(CPUs, 16). gui.sh runs ctest --parallel ZERUS_TEST_JOBS (default min(CPUs, 8)); test_sessionswindow runs as 10 shards via tray/tests/RunQtShard.cmake (functions assigned by name hash). Measured here: CLI suite ~5 min -> ~31 s (Python 286 s -> 23 s), Qt suite ~157 s -> ~24 s; three CLI and three Qt runs green. Remaining floor: single tests with real timers (accounts transfer deadline 20 s, codex async queued answers 14 s, git context cache 15 s, sessionswindow nativeLaunch 21 s).
close_reason: Closed

title: Prepare mobile service for a public managed launch
description: The Android pilot and self-hostable relay are implemented. Before offering a paid managed service, add account/workspace enrollment and deletion, production Android signing and release distribution, operator-owned FCM provisioning, quotas/monitoring/backups and independent security review. Design verified computer pairing and end-to-end encrypted session payloads before promising a cloud operator cannot read customer content. Preserve the open-source self-hostable protocol. See docs/mobile-architecture.md and docs/mobile-deployment.md.

title: Serialize service and launcher startup around the GUI socket
description: The GUI performs a single-instance probe and then removes/listens on the shared socket without serializing concurrent starts. A standalone --sessions launch immediately after restarting systemd/launchd can claim that socket first, leaving the managed GUI exited while the standalone workspace remains open. This was reproduced during draft deployment. Serialize startup and forward activation only after the owning service socket is ready, preserving durable drafts and native agent lifetimes.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent service/launcher starts leave one service-owned GUI; activation opens its workspace without a second owner, arbitrary process termination or native agent restarts; stale sockets can still recover after a crash.
close_reason: Merged in PR #60

title: Publish first public Arch/AUR release after owner decisions
description: Publish the first public Zerus 0.37.0 Arch x86_64 distribution from a reviewed exact-source candidate. Owner confirmed public upstream ufna/zerus, ufna as primary AUR maintainer with public attribution, zerus (stable source), zerus-git (main VCS), zerus-ade-bin (binary), explicit zerus-setup and manual-only CI. Dedicated AUR SSH identity and main-only GitHub release environment are configured. Remaining work is an explicitly owner-requested candidate run, candidate review, manual GitHub/AUR publication and a fresh public yay installation/desktop-agent upgrade roundtrip.

title: Recognize project worktrees in the new-session folder preview
description: A new or existing linked worktree selected for a project is presented as an outside-project folder because the preview only tests saved folder IDs. Recognize verified worktree catalogs belonging to the selected project and machine, while preserving warnings for unrelated folders and keeping launch-only folder selections local to the dialog.
design: Require an available non-bare checkout catalog containing both the selected path and a saved project folder on the selected machine. Keep successful creation evidence in the dialog until the refreshed catalog catches up; recheck it against current project folders. Preserve project catalogs and normal folder launch behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Created and selected linked worktrees show a neutral project-worktree preview. Unrelated repositories and plain folders retain the warning. Project and machine changes cannot reuse stale membership evidence. Synthetic local and remote cases pass.
notes: Verified worktree catalogs now connect the selected folder to saved project folders on the same machine. Successful creation retains dialog-local membership until catalog refresh; unrelated, bare and unavailable folders keep the warning. Existing-picker, new-worktree, subdirectory, project-switch and machine-switch checks passed (10 worktree-panel checks on Linux and macOS), along with the full Linux GUI suites and affected macOS window scenarios. No project folders or worktrees are created implicitly.
close_reason: Both GUI corrections are implemented, tested on Linux and macOS, and installed on the development machines. Native sessions and CLI binaries were preserved.

title: Render native question replies as readable Activity answer cards
description: Codex optional-question replies appear in Activity as a raw send_user_message_question_reply envelope with JSON and transport IDs. Render recognized replies with a clear question and answer, preserving literal content and message identity. Keep unrecognized or malformed messages intact and do not change native delivery.
acceptance_criteria: Known native reply envelopes render readable question/answer cards without exposed transport markup. Escaping, unsupported input fallback and existing Activity behavior are covered by synthetic tests. Deploy and push the approved correction.
notes: Implemented readable native reply cards for journal, recorded context, local delivery and search. Question context is muted; the literal answer has its own highlighted section. Strict envelope/schema recognition preserves malformed or example input, and escaping prevents markup/resources from becoming active. Full Activity suites passed on Linux and macOS (89 tests each, one existing preview skip); synthetic light/dark previews remain outside Git. Installed both GUIs and verified build identity, running services, unchanged CLI binaries and native process identities.
close_reason: Readable answer cards were validated on Linux and macOS, deployed with native process preservation, and pushed to origin/main as 2f62568. Synthetic previews remain outside Git.

title: Support native DeepSeek context reset when available
description:
## Summary

Clear context is intentionally disabled for DeepSeek because the integrated native SessionController has no supported reset method. Add a capability-gated native reset when the upstream interface supports it. Preserve conversation identity and never truncate provider-owned history or replace a running agent.

## Acceptance Criteria

The supported native operation works from Zerus with exact session identity, preserves user data and has regression coverage. Unsupported native versions retain an explicit safe fallback.
close_reason: Not supported by the pinned @deepseek-ai/dsh 0.2.0-rc.2: no SessionController reset method, no native /clear or /new command, no runtime context-reset event (static API and isolated keyless probe). Clear stays an explicit refusal, pinned by a test in PR #129; revisit when the upstream canary reports a newer dsh.

title: Avoid executing custom launchers during capability detection
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

Run the custom-launcher cases in tests/test_pause.py.

## Actual Behavior

The Codex capability probe in src/state/lifecycle.rs invokes the configured executable with --help before a supervised run exists. Custom launchers may block, exit, or produce side effects before run identity is recorded. Detect capabilities without executing a user wrapper outside supervision. Cover failed, cancelled and requested-conversation startup in tests/test_pause.py.

## Expected Behavior

Launchers run only inside supervision and failures retain the intended run identity.

## Acceptance Criteria

Regression tests reproduce the original condition and pass reliably after a verified fix, without bypassing identity checks or relying on another account.
close_reason: Merged in PR #59

title: Publish Zerus to winget
description:
Make Zerus installable with winget. This does not depend on signing.

- WinGet 1.5 and later accept a zip with NestedInstallerType portable, so start with the existing portable zip and switch to the installer once it exists.
- Submit the manifest by PR to microsoft/winget-pkgs (wingetcreate) for stable releases only, not nightlies.
- The owner chooses the package identifier.
- Any publication token stays in the release environment, and publication stays owner-triggered.
- Before the first submission, check the winget-pkgs validation policy for unsigned packages.

Owner 2026-10-17: winget now (reactivated from the deferred epic); identifier ufna.Zerus, stable only, portable zip with ArchiveBinariesDependOnPath.
2026-10-17: implementation in PR 199 (branch windows-winget); fork ufna/winget-pkgs created; first submission microsoft/winget-pkgs PR 454847 opened by scripts/publish-winget.py; rerun verified idempotent. Follow-ups: zerus-qxdx.6 (owner token/CLA), zerus-qxdx.7 (user docs after acceptance).

title: Self-update installer-based Windows builds from the update feed
description:
Let installer builds update themselves.

Feed:
- The v1 feed rejects unknown artifact kinds, and schema 2 has no Windows kind. Add the Windows installer through a new schema or endpoint that older GUIs never read, and keep v1 unchanged.

Update flow:
1. Download the installer to a private temporary folder with a size bound.
2. Verify the size and SHA-256 against the feed.
3. On signed channels, verify Authenticode with WinVerifyTrust against the expected publisher.
4. Unsigned nightlies are still checked against the feed hash. Orca skips verification entirely for its unsigned dev channel; we keep the hash check.
5. Save drafts, as tray/update-installed.py does.
6. Start the installer silently and exit the GUI. The installer relaunches it.
7. If the update fails, the current installation stays intact.

Channels:
- The installed build identity stays independent of the selected channel.
- Portable builds keep link-only behavior.
- Dev has no Windows build unless it is added explicitly.

Updates never stop agents or the session host. All I/O is bounded and runs in the background.

title: Sign the Windows portable zip executables during publication
description:
Sign every Zerus-built PE file in the Windows portable zip (hgs.exe, hgs-tray.exe and any helpers we build) before the zip is sealed. Skip files that already carry a valid signature, as Orca does.

- SHA256SUMS and release-info.json are computed after signing.
- For signed channels, CI checks Get-AuthenticodeSignature for status Valid and the expected subject.
- Signing runs only on trusted main, in a dedicated environment.
- Submission and waiting are bounded. A retry signs the same verified candidate and never rebuilds or overwrites published assets.
- The staged stable CLI (.local/bin/hgs.exe) is a copy of the signed hgs.exe, so hooks start a signed binary. That reduces Smart App Control and WDAC blocks.
- Update docs/public-distribution.md, the SmartScreen text in docs/installation.md and, for SignPath, the code signing policy page.

Acceptance:
- A signed release zip passes the CI signature checks.
- Unsigned channels stay documented.
- Retries reuse the same candidate.
notes: Owner 2026-10-17: never change the signature of a bundled third-party binary. Sign only Zerus-built PE files (hgs.exe, hgs-tray.exe and helpers we build); leave vcruntime140*.dll, msvcp140.dll, Qt and FFmpeg DLLs, conpty.dll and OpenConsole.exe byte-identical whether they are signed or not. CI must check those files are unchanged after signing (same hashes as the unsigned build).

title: Ship a per-user Windows installer beside the portable zip
description:
Publish a per-user installer next to the portable zip.

Tool: Inno Setup (Zed, VS Code) or NSIS (Orca, OBS).

Install:
- No elevation (PrivilegesRequired=lowest); installs into %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Zerus.
- Start menu shortcut, uninstaller and a silent mode for updates.
- Only the downloaded installer carries Mark of the Web, so SmartScreen appears at most once. Later in-app downloads do not carry it.

Isolation:
- The installer never touches host images, the stable CLI, config or state.
- It closes only hgs-tray from the install folder. The session host runs from its staged image, so it keeps running.

Assets and verification:
- zerus-<version>-windows-x86_64-setup.exe is sealed in SHA256SUMS and named in release-info.json.
- Extend the release_common and nightly_common validation and the update_feed.py asset family. Redeploy the mirror before the first release that carries the installer, as zerus-5qaa did for the zip.
- With SignPath, signing takes two stages: inner files, then the installer.

Tests:
- A disposable-runner E2E, like Orca's win-update-survival: install release N, start a local session, silently install N+1 over it, then assert that the host PID is unchanged and the session is still interactive.
- Uninstall leaves the host images and sessions as documented.

UpdateController tells installer builds apart from portable ones.

title: Decide the Windows code signing provider and release approval cadence
description:
Choose who signs Windows binaries, which channels are signed and who approves each release.

SignPath Foundation (free OSS program; signpath.org/terms verified 2026-10-17):
- "Every release needs manual approval for signing."
- A project team member trusted by the team approves, not SignPath staff. SignPath's own review happens once, when the project applies.
- All team members need MFA for both SignPath and GitHub.
- Origin verification requires builds on GitHub-hosted runners.
- The certificate shows "SignPath Foundation" as publisher.
- A "Code signing policy" (roles and privacy policy) must appear on the home and download pages.
- "The project may not contain any proprietary, non open-source component." Ask whether the app-local Microsoft VC++ runtime DLLs in the zip qualify (vcruntime140.dll, vcruntime140_1.dll, msvcp140.dll; already Microsoft-signed). If not, decide between a static CRT and the system redistributable. Unsigned upstream OSS DLLs such as Qt are allowed. The Foundation may later require that every included file be signed.

Release cadence:
- 11 stable desktop releases between 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-16 (v0.38.0 to v0.44.0), up to 4 in one day.
- Zip-only means one approval per stable, because SignPath signs PE files inside a zip. An installer means two approvals: inner files first, then the installer.
- Publication waits for the approval.
- Daily nightlies need a daily approval or stay unsigned, as Orca's dev channels do.

Azure Artifact Signing:
- No per-release human approval; it fits nightly automation.
- The publisher is our verified name.
- Needs an eligible organization (USA, Canada, EU, UK) or individual (USA, Canada) and a paid Azure subscription.
- About $9.99 a month for 5,000 signatures.

OV certificate: cloud HSM or token key, renewal at least every 460 days. Its SmartScreen reputation behaves the same as Azure's.

Acceptance: the owner records the provider, the signed channels and the approvers, and the decision is stored with bd remember.
notes: Owner 2026-10-17 on SignPath: «dll класть можно, нельзя на них подпись менять!» Bundling third-party DLLs (app-local MSVC runtime, Qt, FFmpeg, ConPTY pair) is acceptable; their signatures must never be changed. This settles the MSVC runtime question for the SignPath option.

title: Windows distribution: code signing, per-user installer, self-update and winget
description:
Owner direction 2026-10-17: research how other vendors ship Windows desktop apps and record the plan, but do not implement it yet. The portable zip stays the Windows distribution for now.

Current state (verified 2026-10-17): stable releases after 0.42.2 and nightlies carry the unsigned portable zip zerus-<version>-windows-x86_64.zip (v0.44.0 has it). The zip is a GitHub-only asset. The portable GUI defaults to the nightly channel and reads the zerus.dev v1 desktop feed (updates/v1/desktop/<channel>.json, which the mirror builds from GitHub Releases) at most once a day. When a newer product version carries a Windows zip, it links that GitHub release page. There is no installer and no self-update. SmartScreen warns on first start. Smart App Control on Windows 11 blocks unsigned apps with no per-app exemption. AppLocker, WDAC or ASR rules may block the staged hgs.exe that hooks start (see the antivirus and enterprise policy risk in the Windows native host spec).

Research summary (2026-10-17):
- Orca (stablyai/orca, Electron): one per-user NSIS installer, with no zip, MSI or MSIX. Release builds are signed through the SignPath Foundation OSS program in two requests: first the inner PE files including the uninstaller, then the rebuilt installer. Each request needs manual approval; Orca budgets 1 h + 4 h, on GitHub-hosted runners. electron-updater reads GitHub Releases latest.yml + blockmap and checks the Authenticode publisherName. Hourly/daily dev channels ship unsigned with that verification disabled. A release stays a draft until every platform asset exists. A disposable-runner E2E proves the daemon survives an update.
- Zed (Rust): Inno Setup installer signed through Azure Trusted Signing. auto_update_helper.exe swaps files after exit using Restart Manager, with rollback jobs.
- VS Code: Inno Setup user and system installers plus a zip. OBS (Qt): NSIS installer plus its own updater using a manifest and zstd delta patches. Telegram Desktop (Qt): Inno Setup installer plus portable build, with its own updater and signed update packages. Wireshark (Qt): WinSparkle with an Ed25519-signed appcast. KeePassXC (Qt): WiX MSI plus portable zip.
- Signing (Microsoft Learn "Code signing options for Windows app developers", updated 2026-08-29): Azure Artifact Signing costs about $9.99 a month and is open to organizations in the USA, Canada, EU and UK, and to individuals in the USA and Canada only. An OV certificate costs $150-300 a year; its key must sit on an HSM or token since June 2023, and validity is at most 460 days from 2026-03-01. EV certificates lost the instant SmartScreen bypass in 2024. SmartScreen reputation always builds over time.

Constraints for every child:
- Updates never stop agents, session hosts, tmux or resident adapters.
- An installer never touches the content-addressed host images (.local/share/hgs/host), the stable CLI (.local/bin/hgs.exe), or config and state.
- The portable zip stays available.
- Feed compatibility holds: the v1 feed rejects unknown artifact kinds, so new Windows assets stay out of v1.
- Stable publication stays owner-triggered; nightlies stay automatic after full CI.
- Signing credentials live only in a main-only environment and never reach PR code.
- No paid runners.
acceptance_criteria: The owner reactivates the epic; each child closes with its own acceptance. Until then the portable zip remains the Windows distribution.

title: Flaky macOS CI: TestActivityView::voiceWaveformSeeksWithoutRelayout(normal)
description: Main CI run 39030964535 (commit 4a82c63d, a docs and Beads change) failed the signed macOS dev candidate job only on 'before!=document->resource(QTextDocument::ImageResource,image.first).value<QImage>()' in voiceWaveformSeeksWithoutRelayout(normal); the same test passed on the PR run and on the previous main run. title: iOS: notification service extension for detailed cards while Zerus is closed
description: Follow-up to iOS #8. APNs wakes show the generic content-free alert 'New session activity.' and Zerus replaces it with detailed session cards when iOS lets the app run (content-available, background refresh or the next open). A Notification Service Extension (mutable-content is already set by the relay) could perform the authenticated event and catalog reads itself and rewrite the alert into the session card before display, matching Android's data-wake behavior even when the app was force-quit. Needs: an extension target and provisioning, a shared Keychain access group for the gateway credential, a shared sealed notification state with cross-process coordination, and the same policy so the app and extension never double-announce.

title: tmux scope unit test a_refused_scope_never_runs_the_command flakes on output().unwrap() under load
description: Seen once by the zerus-etoy reviewer (2026-10-15) during a full cargo test run while native Claude module runs loaded the host: src/state/backend/tmux/scope.rs a_refused_scope_never_runs_the_command panicked on .output().unwrap() (the spawn itself failed). Passed alone 3 times and in the next full run. Suspected cause: ETXTBSY. fake_systemd_run writes the fixture script with fs::write and then executes it; a concurrent test thread that forks while the write fd is open keeps that fd until its exec, so exec of the fixture fails with 'Text file busy'. Confirm the errno under parallel load before fixing (e.g. retry on ErrorKind::ExecutableFileBusy, or run fixtures through /bin/sh).
notes:
Agent workflow wf_07ec63da-cec, worktree private:worktree/zerus-fix-scope-txtbsy
Confirmed ETXTBSY (os error 26), 23/300 -> 0/300. PR #151.
close_reason: Merged in #151: platform::write_script (test-only) lets /bin/sh write executable fixtures so the test process never holds their write descriptor; ETXTBSY 23/300 -> 0/300.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text: Related hosted evidence: main CI 38813489733 attempt 1 (source f16d73bc) failed registered_version_is_read_again_only_for_another_executable at hooks.rs:1887, returning None for the first version probe. The swallowed probe error was not printed, so that exact failure does not independently prove ETXTBSY. PR151 changes the affected fixture writer. The isolated macOS test passed; the same hosted candidate is being retried without bypassing any checks.

title: Decide whether request bodies with lone UTF-16 surrogates are refused
description: The Rust relay refuses any body containing a lone UTF-16 surrogate escape with 400; the Python reference relay accepted one, for example in a heartbeat snapshot. Confirm no released client sends such escapes (Android, the Python connector from snapshot text) before treating the refusal as the contract. Recorded under 'Differences found' in services/mobile/relay/tests/ORACLE.md (zerus-3rqx.5). Decide whether the Rust behaviour is the contract; production already runs the Rust relay.

title: Decide the error text for a workspace over its retained-payload budget
description: Both relays answer 429, but the Python reference relay's message named the retained payload while the Rust relay says 'relay capacity is busy'. Android shows receipt and error text to the user. Recorded under 'Differences found' in services/mobile/relay/tests/ORACLE.md (zerus-3rqx.5). Decide whether the Rust behaviour is the contract; production already runs the Rust relay.

title: Decide whether authenticated requests need global and per-address limits
description: The Python reference relay also limited authenticated requests globally and per IP address; the Rust relay limits them per credential (2,400 a minute) plus admission lanes. Check that this is enough for a shared public relay behind the reverse proxy. Recorded under 'Differences found' in services/mobile/relay/tests/ORACLE.md (zerus-3rqx.5). Decide whether the Rust behaviour is the contract; production already runs the Rust relay.

title: Refuse answers with integers the connector cannot parse at submission
description: Found by the P3 review (zerus-3rqx.3): the Rust relay's protocol::request accepts an answer whose answers hold a 4,301-digit integer, but the connector's request parser refuses integers over 4,300 digits (Python's int max-str-digits limit, MAX_INT_DIGITS in the Rust connector). Such a request is queued, then fails to parse on the computer and the claim expires as uncertain instead of the phone getting an immediate 400. Make the relay refuse the same bound at submission and add a vector at 4,300/4,301 digits.

title: Decide whether DEL (U+007F) is refused in session, computer and run identities
description: Found by the P3 golden-vector check (zerus-3rqx.3): the Rust relay's protocol::text refuses DEL (U+007F) in session, computer_id and the expected_run_id/expected_conversation_id of send/answer/interrupt, while the Python reference relay and the Python connector accept it there (ORACLE_DIFFERENCES rows session/delete, computer-id/delete, payload/run-delete in services/mobile/relay/tests/vectors.rs). Both relays accept DEL in an answer's question_id and expected_question_hash. Decide one rule (recommended: treat DEL like the other control characters everywhere identities are checked, matching the Rust relay) and make the Rust connector, the relay and the vectors agree; the Python connector only needs the change if it outlives the cutover.

title: test_account_mcp teardown intermittently fails with Directory not empty on Ubuntu CI
description: Seen on 2026-10-15 in two unrelated PRs (#102 run 38787850240 job 116604444075 and #132): tests/test_account_mcp.py ManagedProfileMcp.test_claude_and_kimi_profiles_receive_native_servers errors in stop() at self.temp.cleanup(): shutil.rmtree fails in os.rmdir (Directory not empty), so some process still writes into the test's temp tree after the private tmux server is killed and its panes are gone (ea4f5e66 already waits for the panes). Find the writer (a detached hgs worker such as recovery/voice/swarm, a hook process, an agent stand-in child) and make the test stop or wait for it, or make cleanup robust without hiding a real leak.
notes: PR #138 (fix/account-mcp-teardown): stop() waits for pane descendants (dash keeps sh -c as pane pid on Ubuntu; hgs --run supervisor writes its record after the shell exits).
close_reason: Merged in #138 (de04b42f): test_account_mcp stop() waits for the pane processes and all their descendants before removing the fixture; on Ubuntu dash keeps sh -c as the pane pid while the hgs --run supervisor finishes its session record.

title: test_single_overwrites_wrapped_draft_from_cursor_middle intermittently reports 'terminal changed while preparing the answer'
description: Found in the final verification on 2026-10-15: tests/test_claude_questions_native.py NativeClaudeQuestions.test_single_overwrites_wrapped_draft_from_cursor_middle against pinned Claude Code 2.1.296 fails about 1 in 3 parallel module runs on plain origin/main (72278ce3) with 'hgs: delivery uncertain: terminal changed while preparing the answer; inspect it before retrying'. Also seen once in a full agent-compatibility.py --agent claude run. Find what changes the terminal while hgs prepares the answer (Claude redraw of the wrapped draft, cursor blink, spinner) and make the preparation robust without weakening the changed-terminal safety check.
notes: PR #148 (fix/claude-question-flake), rebased; native Claude 2.1.296 matrix 61/61 on the rebased branch.

title: Retire divergence c in the design spec and vector notes
description: Main's peer callback fix (cc42fff9, max_output_bytes through fleet.py) makes the Python connector complete a peer attachment_read through the peer, so divergence c no longer differs. The black-box suites already expect the completed read from both connectors (mobile/connector-bb-suites). Update docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-15-rust-mobile-connector-design.md (row c and its notes), services/mobile/vectors/README.md and the divergence_c note produced by capture.py (receipts.json) so they no longer describe the old Python failure. Also map main's file_read (test_computer_file_read.py) into BLACKBOX.md with a black-box suite in C4.

title: Android: check pending settings for the scheduled-apply race fixed on the desktop
description: The desktop fix for zerus-4ccz retries a pending settings change once per Ready transition when an automatic apply comes back 'scheduled' (a terminal chooser appeared between the idle listing and the dispatch; see PR #125 for the CLI side). Android has its own pending-settings logic in mobile/android and was not checked for the same race. For the Android owner: verify whether a 'scheduled' result drops the change from Android's automatic apply and align with the desktop behaviour if so.

title: Desktop drops a pending settings change from automatic apply when dispatch schedules it
description: Found in zerus-ona8 (PR #125): tray/src/SessionsWindow.cpp records each automatic pending-apply attempt in m_settingsAttempts and removes the entry from its queue when the result is 'scheduled'. If a terminal chooser appears in the short gap between the listing showing idle and the dispatch, the pending change gets no further automatic retry; it stays pending until the next message or a manual apply. Keep a scheduled pending change eligible for the next automatic apply once the listing shows idle/idle and inspect reports settings_apply_when now, without retry storms (one attempt per Ready transition).
close_reason: Merged in PR #127: the desktop retries a scheduled pending settings change once per Ready transition.

title: Inspect offers fork and immediate settings while a terminal chooser blocks them
description: Found in the zerus-4vty review (PR #123): while a terminal-only chooser is visible (kimi_cache_hint, codex_goal_resume, a trust or update panel), inspect still reports fork_supported true and settings_apply_when now. Dispatch refuses the fork in checked_ready, and a settings change fails with the chooser error instead of being scheduled; no keys are sent. Align inspect with dispatch as PR #123 did for clear and compaction (use the summary's chooser result in fork::summary and effort::summary: fork unsupported with the chooser reason, settings_apply_when ready so the change is scheduled), and make dispatch_settings schedule rather than fail when a chooser blocks an immediate apply.
close_reason: Merged in PR #125: while a terminal chooser waits, fork is held back with its reason and settings changes are scheduled instead of failing; no keys reach the chooser.

title: Dispatch, fork and effort gates count a stale Kimi hook child as busy
description: Found in the zerus-1qnm review (PR #115): input::checked_ready (clear/compact/settings dispatch), fork::unavailable and effort::ready treat any child with state working as busy, while the listing, pause and the clear/compact reason use telemetry::child_working, which skips non-native Kimi hook entries once kimi_native_roster is set. If profile SubagentStop hooks are missed after the native catalog takes over, an old combined hook entry stays working: the listing shows Ready and clear/compact are reported available, but dispatch refuses ('agent is busy or waiting for approval'), and fork and settings are blocked the same way. Make these gates use telemetry::work_remains / child_working. Also: the saved-record clear gate does not consider terminal-only choosers such as kimi_cache_hint (summary() shows them as busy); dispatch rejects them through checked_input, so check that inspect reports them consistently.
close_reason: Merged in PR #123: dispatch, fork, settings and effort gates use telemetry::settled like the listing; inspect reports terminal choosers in clear and compaction reasons.

title: Clear and compaction report available for a Kimi session whose profile groups still work
description: Found in the zerus-1crv review (PR #114): clear_context::available() reads the raw record activity, so a Kimi session with active profile groups but idle raw activity reports clear and compaction as available although the session (per its aggregated status) still works. Use the same aggregated busy state the listing shows (profile groups, active tools, children) when gating clear and compaction, with tests.
close_reason: Merged in PR #115: clear and compaction stay unavailable while Kimi profile groups work; reasons name groups as the listing does.

title: Explain why Compact and Clear context are unavailable in the desktop
description: Follow-up from zerus-rwiw (PR #108): when Compact and continue or Clear context are disabled because a child or tool still works, the desktop gives no reason. Show the blocking reason (e.g. which child or tool is still working) in the cold-cache dialog or the disabled action's tooltip, from data the inspect/listing already provides (clear_context_supported / compact_context_supported and the subagent states).
close_reason: Merged in PR #114: inspect reports why clear and compaction are unavailable; the desktop shows the reason.

title: Docs say Codex Escape may start a queued follow-up, but pinned Codex leaves ordinary follow-ups unsent
description: Follow-up from the zerus-5ok review (PR #111): docs/reference.md (around the Codex queue paragraph) says 'Codex Escape may start a queued follow-up', but a keyless probe of the pinned Codex 0.160.1/0.162.0 showed that with only ordinary follow-ups queued, Escape (and so Stop) leaves them as one unsent composer draft. Correct the docs and check what Stop reports to the user in that case (Activity/receipt); if Stop claims a follow-up was started, fix the wording or behaviour.
close_reason: Merged in PR #113: docs say Stop leaves ordinary Codex follow-ups as an unsent draft; pinned panel fixtures added.

title: Voice worker service can respawn every few seconds while a detached worker holds its lock
description: Follow-up from the zerus-hhx4 review (PR #110): src/state/voice.rs has the same exit-0-on-held-lock pattern the recovery worker had. If the voice service is managed with KeepAlive/Restart and a detached voice worker holds the lock, the managed one is restarted indefinitely. Apply the PR #110 approach (service worker waits holding a service lock; detached worker yields) if the voice service is restarted on exit; otherwise document why not. Also review PR #110's Linux service identity check (cgroup leaf hgs-recovery.service): a detached worker spawned by a process inside that service's cgroup would be taken for the service worker.
close_reason: Merged in PR #112: the voice service's worker waits instead of respawning; the Linux service identity uses the unit's MainPID.

title: Reject direct QProcess starts in tray/src outside ChildProcess.h
description: Follow-up from zerus-lvon (PR #98): after PRs #93 and #98 every Unix child start in tray/src goes through ChildProcess::inheritStdioOnly or ChildProcess::startDetached. Add a scripts/ci/check-source.py rule that rejects new direct QProcess start()/startDetached()/execute() calls in tray/src outside ChildProcess.h (allowing WindowsTerminalBackend.cpp and calls preceded by inheritStdioOnly), with a test of the rule, so the macOS pipe inheritance race cannot come back.
close_reason: Merged in PR #101: check-source rejects desktop child starts that bypass ChildProcess.h.

title: Smoke check 'failed attach, server alive' times out under load
description: Found in the zerus-n590 stress runs (2026-10-15): with 6 parallel tests/test_hgs.sh copies under 24 busy loops, the check 'failed attach, server alive' (tests/test_hgs.sh around lines 308-316) sometimes fails with an empty rc because wait_rc2 times out: 4 of 12 runs on the old binary, 1 of 6 on the fixed one. It is in the attach/server-death path, not the listing. Find whether the attach failure is slow (product) or the wait budget is too tight (test), and fix the real cause.
close_reason: Merged in PR #99: isolated tmux servers are awaited after kill-server before their socket is reused.

title: Delete the stale desktop update surface exporter
description: scripts/export-desktop-updates.py and scripts/desktop_update_surface.py were a one-off integration exporter from 2d66887. Their source anchors no longer exist in main (SettingsPage.h has no 'tr("Processes"),tr("About")' anchor; tray/CMakeLists.txt uses qt_add_executable and already defines hgs-updates), and nothing else imports them. Remove both files and the docs block that runs them (docs/public-distribution.md around line 440-456).
notes: PR #104 (chore/remove-desktop-update-exporter), reviewed; awaiting CI.
close_reason: Merged in PR #104 (955c739); main CI 38740582425 green.

title: Report every mirror publisher transport and archive failure with the fixed log line
description: The publisher entry points catch only ValueError, OSError, KeyError, TypeError, UnicodeError and zipfile.BadZipFile (scripts/publish-update-feed.py:101, publish-dev-feed.py:80, receive-dev-token.py:57), and the stream loop maps only OSError (scripts/update_feed.py:95-96). http.client.IncompleteRead (an HTTPException, e.g. a truncated chunked GitHub response), tarfile.TarError, EOFError and zlib.error are not subclasses of these, so they escape as a Python traceback instead of 'Mirror validation or transport failed; previous catalogs retained'. Publication still fails closed. Catch these types (or add a final catch-all with the same fixed message), add an explicit Python 3.11 version check matching docs/public-distribution.md, and make publish-dev-feed.py print its failure line to stderr. After merge the zerus.dev mirror needs the usual --tags mirror redeploy (see zerus-5qaa).
notes: Merged in PR #103 (e39aa7b); main CI green. Remaining: --tags mirror redeploy of all five publisher files, awaiting owner approval (asked 2026-10-15).
close_reason: Merged in PR #103 and deployed 2026-10-16 (owner: «да -- по обоим пунктам») by the hgdev-infra session from zerus main 229f734: check mode changed only the four non-update_feed files (update_feed.py had already been deployed on 2026-10-15 19:43 MSK by an unattributed --tags mirror run); on-host sha256 of all five files match; desktop-stable, desktop-nightly and android-dev runs succeeded; public v1/v2 catalogs verified; rollback copy at /root/zerus-updates.pre-229f734-20261016/.

title: UpdateController's direct child starts bypass the stdio-only helper
description: Follow-up from zerus-bojp (PR #93): tray/src/UpdateController.cpp still starts two children directly (the restart /bin/sh startDetached and a new QProcess), which were frozen by PR #86 when the helper landed. Route them through ChildProcess::inheritStdioOnly / ChildProcess::startDetached so they cannot inherit ProcessRunner pipe ends on macOS.
close_reason: Merged in PR #98: UpdateController's restart helper and package probes start with only stdio.

title: Verify actual font scaling in Android dialog smoke fixtures
description: While qualifying zerus-wdi1, an outer LocalDensity fixture override did not visibly enlarge text inside the Android dialog window. NativeSettingsLayoutSmokeInstrumentation now overrides density inside each dialog slot and asserts that the rendered Model heading grows by at least1.4x for180% text. Audit existing dialog fixtures, especially DialogActionsSmokeInstrumentation, which uses the outer-provider pattern, and verify actual native text growth before accepting large-font coverage. Keep this scoped to test validity; do not alter runtime settings or live device data.

title: test_draft_unknown_model_and_identity_fail_without_input times out waiting for the draft on macOS
description: PR #83 rerun of run 38644000007, macOS CLI job 116133101658 (2026-10-14): tests/test_settings.py:288 wait_for('draft' in capture-pane) failed with 'fixture timed out' (test_input.py:132). Same tmux input harness as zerus-sqsb (test_claude_nbsp_prompt..., also macOS). Find whether typed fixture text reaches the pane late on macOS runners (send-keys timing, fixture startup, the wait_for budget) or is lost, and fix the shared cause.
close_reason: Merged in PR #107: fixture agents wait in select() with signal.set_wakeup_fd, so a SIGUSR1 redraw that lands before read() blocks is no longer lost (13 fixtures).

title: test_failed_resume_keeps_binding_and_no_fresh_fallback hits a session row without state
description: PR #84 run 38644206929, Ubuntu CLI job 116127008636 (2026-10-14): tests/test_pause.py:649 snapshot['sessions'][0]['state'] raised KeyError: the listing row for the session had no state at that moment. The PR only changed the desktop. Find why hgs ls can list the session without a state right after a failed resume (a transient tmux-only row before the record merges? a race with the failed resume cleanup?), decide whether that is a product bug (a listing should always carry state for a tracked session) or a test wait issue, and fix accordingly.
close_reason: Merged in PR #97: a session that ends between list-sessions and list-panes is listed with its saved state; the failed-resume test waits for the end.

title: test_claude_nbsp_prompt_accepts_docx_without_overwriting_drafts flakes on macOS
description: PR #83 run 38644000007, macOS CLI job 116126843634 (2026-10-14): tests/test_input.py:607 send returned 1: 'hgs: terminal has a draft, dialog, or unrecognized prompt; open Terminal and return to an empty agent prompt'. The PR only changed src/dsh/bridge.mjs, so the input transport test is intermittent on macOS. Find whether the fixture's NBSP prompt screen is captured before it settles (timing) or the prompt recognizer mis-reads a partial frame, and fix the test wait or the recognizer without weakening the draft-protection assertions.
close_reason: Merged in PR #96: input test screens wait for a unique OSC 2 title with the cursor, not the cursor alone.

title: Claude PostModelSwitch entry stays after a downgrade and blocks older Claude at start
description: Follow-up from zerus-coik (PR #89): once registered, the PostModelSwitch hook entry is never removed, so a Claude older than 2.1.296 later run against the same config dir shows a blocking Settings Warning at every start. hgs already reads the version on every launch while the event is not registered; when it reads a version below the gate and finds the hgs-owned PostModelSwitch entry, remove that entry (only hgs's own hook command, never user entries) before launch.
close_reason: Merged in PR #94: an older Claude gets hgs's PostModelSwitch entry removed before a tracked launch.

title: GUI on macOS: direct QProcess children can inherit ProcessRunner pipe ends
description: Follow-up from zerus-sllg (PR #87): on macOS tray ProcessRunner creates its pipes on a worker thread with pipe() then fcntl(FD_CLOEXEC) (pipeAbove2), while HgsClient starts direct QProcess children on the main thread (machine setup, transfers and others, HgsClient.cpp ~465, 1220, 1345, 1468-1639). Qt forks those without closing inherited fds, so one can inherit a runner child's stdin write end and hold that hgs request open until it exits. Fix with QProcess::setUnixProcessParameters(CloseFileDescriptors) where Qt >= 6.6, or route those children through ProcessRunner, or create runner pipes under a lock shared with QProcess starts.
close_reason: Merged in PR #93: desktop direct QProcess children get only stdio (CloseFileDescriptors on Qt >= 6.8.3).

title: Desktop: a failure callback after an ended launch shows a nameless error
description: Follow-up from the zerus-19do review (PR #82): if a listing reports a launch ended and a failure callback (nativeSessionLaunched with ok=false) arrives afterwards, newSessionLaunchFailed replaces the ended notice; the pending launch is already gone, so the text reads 'Could not start session : <error>'. More likely for non-detached launches (dsh/opencode). Let the ended notice win (or keep the launch name). Also m_endedLaunches never shrinks when no callback follows (terminal launches, restored pending launches): bound or prune it.
close_reason: Merged in PR #84: an ended launch's notice stays over a late failure callback; ended launches are bounded.

title: Audit multi-threaded piped spawns for the macOS pipe inheritance race
description: Follow-up from zerus-jb22 (PR #76): on Apple targets Rust std creates Command pipes with pipe() and sets FD_CLOEXEC afterwards, and posix_spawn does not set CLOEXEC_DEFAULT, so a child spawned by one thread can inherit pipe ends another thread is creating; a child holding another child's stdin open blocks EOF-based protocols. PR #76 serializes spawns in mobile_peers::capture_control only. Audit every place hgs (and the GUI helpers it runs) spawns children with piped stdio from more than one thread at a time (thread::spawn, scoped threads, parallel probes, swarm transports, account probes, speech) and apply a shared spawn lock or fd hygiene where concurrent spawns are possible.
close_reason: Merged in PR #87: concurrent spawners share platform::spawn_in_turn on macOS.

title: Windows host: an ended launch may miss its last screen lines
description: Follow-up from the zerus-ziq3.13 review (PR #67): on the Windows host, launches::screen() captures the supervisor's own pane 100 ms after the agent exits and stops at the first two equal reads. ConPTY output reaches the host asynchronously (the host waits up to 5 s for it to drain before a session ends), so on a slow machine the ended launch's output may lack the last line the agent printed. Use the host's drained output (e.g. launch_status or a host op that returns the final screen after the drain) instead of a fixed settle.
close_reason: Merged in PR #81: the session host completes an ended launch's report from its drained screen; the supervisor's capture stays as fallback.

title: Local ctest runs newsessiondialog on the real desktop
description: 47e4bb2 inserted the newsessiondialog registration between accountusage's zerus_add_test and its offscreen property, so newsessiondialog had no QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen. CI exports offscreen globally (scripts/ci/gui.sh), but a local ctest opened real dialogs and focusWhileCatalogLoadsKeepsRememberedAgent failed at qWaitForWindowActive. Make zerus_add_test default every suite to offscreen and restore the misplaced lines.
close_reason: zerus_add_test now defaults every CTest suite to QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen; newsessiondialog and accountusage set it explicitly again. Local ctest without a global platform: 60/60 twice. Commit 6da99b9; CI main #482 (1bfe528, contains it) succeeded.

title: Git status reports a changed remote when the tracking ref lookup fails or times out
description: Follow-up from the zerus-o0po review: in src/state/git_status.rs, a failed or timed-out rev-parse --verify @{upstream} falls back to an empty tracking OID, so remote_check compares the ls-remote hash with an empty string and reports changed (Remote branch changed. Fetch to update). Correct when the tracking ref is genuinely missing locally, misleading when the lookup merely failed; tell the two apart as the upstream lookup now does.
close_reason: Merged in PR #78: only rev-parse --verify --quiet exit 1 with empty stderr counts as a missing tracking ref; other failures keep remote_state unknown.

title: test_discovery_fanout_transports_exit_after_gateway_kill misses a peer transport on macOS
description: PR #69 run 38620207559, macOS CLI job 116045922510 (2026-10-14): tests/test_mobile_peers.py:424 assertTrue(all(path.exists() for path in paths)) failed: not every discovery-pids-<alias> marker appeared within the 10 s window (already widened in 8609b75). The window equals the discovery deadline, so a peer whose identity transport starts late (local identity, then its own support probe, all separate cold processes) is never launched and the test cannot pass. Find which stage is slow on macOS runners and make the test wait for an observable start condition or give the fixture deadline real margin, without weakening the transport-exit assertions.
close_reason: Merged in PR #76: discovery transports spawn under one lock so macOS workers never inherit each other's pipes; the fan-out test waits for the gateway and requires live transports at the kill.

title: Recovery may free a Codex account slot on task_started before the provider answers
description: Follow-up from the zerus-a1m2 review: occupies() in src/state/recovery.rs treats provider_status_at after the continuation's user_at as progress. Kimi's TurnStarted was excluded (153e68a). A Codex task_started transcript entry also counts as progress but is not treated as a turn start; if Codex writes it after the prompt-submit hook, the account is freed before the provider answers. Verify Codex ordering against the pinned version and fix if confirmed.
close_reason: Not a bug for the pinned Codex 0.160.1 and 0.162.0: RegularTask::run awaits emit_turn_started, which persists and flushes the rollout task_started line before the UserPromptSubmit hook runs, so the line can never count as progress after the continuation's user_at. Only repeated rollout write failures at turn setup could reorder it.

title: TestNewSessionDialog::refreshKeepsSelectionAndLastReportedLimits counts a late limits probe on macOS
description: PR #52 run 38541058974, macOS desktop job 115775710382: test_newsessiondialog.cpp:234 'probes().size()' was 4, expected 3. The same job passed on main at 5562c2a, so this is intermittent. The test was added or changed by 9fdd148 ('Keep launch limits across token refreshes and refresh them on open'). It records probes().size() after Refresh, fires the 60 s timers and expects no new probe within qWait(100). The refresh now also asks for current limits, so a limits probe that started with the Refresh can land inside that 100 ms. Wait for the Refresh's own limits request to finish (or count only probes started after the timers fire) before taking the baseline, without weakening the no-extra-poll assertion.

title: Audit desktop tests that inject inspections while window polls run
description: zerus-oyjg and zerus-1tu8 (PR #44) shared one hazard: a test injects state with HgsClient::inspectionReady while the window's own inspection or poll is still running, and that reply, read from the fixture before the change, lands afterwards and replaces the injected details. On Windows, Qt 6.10 runs coarse timers of 20 ms or less as multimedia timers that post their QTimerEvent (qeventdispatcher_win.cpp), so a confirmation accepted from a 5 ms QTimer shares a sendPostedEvents() batch with queued ProcessRunner replies, and such a reply can arrive before the dialog's exec() returns. Audit tray/tests (test_sessionswindow.cpp first) for tests that inject inspections with the base fixture program() or a fixture whose inspect reply differs from the injected state, or that act on dialogs from short timers, and apply the zerus-a0ak barrier where needed: setDetailsPollForTests plus waiting for the reply to an inspection the test starts itself. Keep every assertion.
notes: 2026-10-14: nightly 38358653846 (2026-10-13, macOS desktop job 115167602965) failed TestSessionsWindow::clearInspectionUpdatesActivityAndCountersImmediately at test_sessionswindow.cpp:1759 ('timeline.indexOf("Earlier answer")>=0' FALSE), likely the same injected-inspection hazard; that flake alone kept the nightly (and its Windows zip) from publishing that day.
close_reason: Merged in PR #79: keepDetailsPollsOut barrier applied to four exposed tests; the nightly failure itself was fixed by 61e1d21.

title: Qualify intermittent cold-cache compaction test failures on Windows
description: TestSessionsWindow::coldCacheCompactWaitsForSuccess(draft) failed once on the windows-desktop job of PR #42 (run 38514870711, job 115691341904): '!composer->editor()->isReadOnly()' returned FALSE at test_sessionswindow.cpp:2238, after a fixed QTest::qWait(100). It passed in the same PR's previous Windows run and the code path (compaction wait on a remote session) is untouched by M6, so it looks timing dependent on a slow runner. Check whether the editor's read-only state is released by an asynchronous apply/poll and replace the fixed wait with QTRY_VERIFY if so.
notes:
Same family on main without M6: Nightly main (8) run 38513713175 at c9bba3a, job 115687746382: TestSessionsWindow::coldCacheConfirmationPreservesDraftAndPinsConversation 'shown' returned FALSE at test_sessionswindow.cpp:1774 (windows-desktop). Both look like fixed waits or window-activation timing on the Windows runner.
Related: zerus-oyjg (in progress) qualifies coldCacheConfirmationPreservesDraftAndPinsConversation on Windows; coordinate with it rather than fixing the same timing twice.
Recurred on PR #42's next Windows run (run 38516396679, job 115696107822) as coldCacheCompactWaitsForSuccess(cancelled), same line 2238 after QTest::qWait(100). M6 does not touch the compaction or composer paths; 2 of 3 Windows runs of that PR hit this test family, main's CI push runs passed and its nightly hit coldCacheConfirmation (zerus-oyjg).
close_reason: Hardened in PR #44 (be17b70), test only; exact cause not reproduced. The editor's read-only state after the draft outcome comes from MessageComposer::updateControls (waiting, draft loading, sending or the window's session-status block, e.g. 'Refresh the session before sending' after a failed inspection, cleared by the next successful one). The fixed qWait(100) became a QTRY_VERIFY2 on !isReadOnly that names the active lock if it persists; the checks that send.json never appears and the text is unchanged stay strict, so a send that held the lock still fails. Windows test PC: unpatched 96/96 for draft and 48/48 for all rows, 0 hits in 120 CI-like shard runs; fixed 96/96. Not folded into zerus-oyjg: different mechanism. Related audit: zerus-a857.

title: Windows host: fall back to inbox ConPTY when the bundled OpenConsole cannot load
description: Review finding from the ConPTY pair packaging (M7), 2026-10-14: OpenConsole.exe of Microsoft.Windows.Console.ConPTY 1.25.260930003 statically imports D3DCOMPILER_47.dll. src/host/conpty.rs picks the bundled pair from file presence plus LoadLibrary of conpty.dll, so on a SKU without D3DCOMPILER_47.dll (Server Core) a 'bundled' host would fail session creation instead of falling back to inbox (spec D6: bundled first, inbox as degraded fallback). Make the pair selection also require D3DCOMPILER_47.dll to load from System32 (or detect OpenConsole's start failure) and fall back to inbox, reporting why in session-host status. Desktop Windows 10/11 ship the DLL, so this is insurance, not a Phase 2 blocker.
notes: PR #45 (2026-10-14): the host reads OpenConsole.exe's PE import table (new portable src/host/pe.rs) and uses inbox ConPTY, logging why, when a load-time DLL (API sets aside) is neither next to the server nor in System32. Verified on the Windows PC: host:: 145/145, test_windows_host 7/7. The reason is in the host's start log, not in session-host status.
close_reason: Merged in PR #45: inbox ConPTY when the bundled OpenConsole.exe imports a DLL this Windows lacks

title: Windows: measure hgs start and hook cost under real-time scanning (S7)
description: Spike S7's scanning half: on a Windows machine with real-time scanning on (Defender or a third-party product), measure hgs.exe start (warm and freshly built image), the whole hook path (a Stop through hgs __state hook) and SQLite journal writes against the 5 s hook timeout. The development PC has no real-time scanning: baseline there is about 11 ms warm start, 25 ms start and 37-38 ms whole hook path (S6, 2026-10-14). Split out of M0 (zerus-ziq3.7.1).
notes: 2026-10-14: the development PC's real-time antivirus is Kaspersky (Security Center productState 0x41000, enabled and up to date); only Defender is off. The S6 and S7-baseline numbers (25 ms bare start, 37-38 ms whole hook path p95 <= 41 ms, 132 ms fresh image, 11 ms warm) were therefore measured under Kaspersky real-time protection, far inside the 5 s hook timeout. No Kaspersky exclusion for the test folders is known. Defender's own real-time scanning remains unmeasured. Spec corrected in PR #55.
close_reason: Measured under Kaspersky real-time protection on the development PC (25 ms bare start, 37-38 ms whole hook path, 132 ms fresh image; far inside the 5 s hook timeout); spec corrected in PR #55. Defender's own real-time scanning remains unmeasured.

While live, the fixed bridge shows an empty page; once stored, every hgs inspect --agent for it fails with 'subagent descriptor is corrupt' (old and new bridge alike). Consider treating a stored child with no own descriptor and no own step/start as never started (empty page) rather than corrupt, keeping real corruption visible.
close_reason: Merged in PR #77: a child with neither descriptor nor step/start is shown as unstarted (empty page) whether live or stored; real corruption stays an error.

title: Codex /clear reset check reads any header above the first prompt row
description: Found in the Windows Phase 2 M4.3 review (2026-10-14), pre-existing on main: clear_context.rs:90 (codex_reset_panel) reads only the rows above the first '›' line, so any Codex screen where the header and folder are still visible above a history prompt or a draft counts as the reset header; only the composer check that follows guards it. Tighten it to the exact post-/clear layout (empty-state panel), with Linux fixtures, as its own change (it alters Linux behaviour).
notes: 2026-10-14: reproduced with real Codex on Linux by the real-agent Windows suite work (zerus-ziq3.7.12): whenever Codex shows the project folder in full in its header (folder outside the home, so not shortened to ~), hgs reports a SessionCleared after the first message and then refuses clear-context. The Linux NativeCodexClear fixture keeps the project under the fixture home, which hides it. Taken by the CI/test-infrastructure session; it blocks gating the windows-host job.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #53 (aa26685). Codex keeps its header above the first history prompt until /clear, so the old reset check (rows above the first '›' row) took a fresh session's answered first message for the reset panel and hgs recorded a false SessionCleared, then refused clear-context. Every new session of real Codex 0.160.1 and 0.162.0 did this; the resumed native fixture hid it. The reset now needs exactly one '›' row, the composer, empty or with one of the two reviewed placeholders, with only the header block above it. Real captures from both pins, Phase 2's 110x35 fixtures and Windows forms in unit tests; a native NativeCodexClear regression (folder outside the fixture home) fails on the old binary for both pins and passes now; full Linux Codex matrix green (12 tests x 4 configs x 2 pins, including rpcv's async question cases); Windows real-agent suite green on the test PC.

Verify that older reviewed Claude versions accept an unknown hook event in settings before adding it to src/state/hooks.rs, and keep PreModelSwitch unregistered: its allow would skip Claude's cache-miss confirmation for the user too.

title: Make subprocessTimeoutLeavesEventLoopResponsive detect a blocked event loop
description: Found in the zerus-fbjy.6 review (2026-10-13). tray/tests/test_updates.cpp subprocessTimeoutLeavesEventLoopResponsive checks a 30 ms single-shot tick with QTRY_VERIFY_WITH_TIMEOUT(tick,1000). Qt 6 QTRY evaluates the expression once more after its loop, so the tick turns true as soon as a blocked loop resumes; neither the old 5 s nor the new 1.5 s package-manager deadline lets the check detect a synchronous probe. Measure the tick's delay with a QElapsedTimer instead, so a blocking probe fails the test.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #18 (merged 0ecd348): subprocessTimeoutLeavesEventLoopResponsive measures the longest pause between 20 ms ticks from before the controller exists and fails above 1 s against the 1.5 s deadline; canonicalOwnershipAsync holds the pacman owner query until the test has seen it start. Both fail with a synchronous probe, also from the constructor (reviewed with mutations).

title: Unlock CLI file locks explicitly instead of relying on handle close
description: On Windows, LockFileEx locks on a closed handle are released by the OS later, at a time that 'depends upon available system resources' (Microsoft LockFileEx docs), so a short-lived hgs process that only drops its lock file can make the next process see contention. state/storage.rs Guard, worktrees.rs and worktree_cleanup.rs already unlock explicitly; metrics.rs was fixed after a Windows CI flake (briefly_held_lock_delays_sampling_instead_of_failing). Remaining sites that only drop the handle: config.rs, machines.rs, accounts.rs (try_lock), accounts/mcp_servers.rs, accounts/claude_settings.rs, mobile_peers.rs (bounded try_lock), swarm/store.rs, swarm/transport.rs (bounded try_lock), state/recovery.rs. Bounded try_lock waits are the ones that can fail. Prefer one shared guard that calls fs2::FileExt::unlock in Drop (UFCS, so Rust 1.89+ std File::unlock is not picked).
close_reason: All fs2 lock sites in src/ now hold platform::FileLock, which unlocks explicitly on drop (state::storage::Guard is an alias). Successful shared worker probes release at once. Regression test: dropping the guard releases the lock while a duplicate handle stays open. Verified locally and on Windows (cargo test, clippy 1.85 -D warnings, Windows client tests).

title: Cached .lnk attachments are judged by their shortcut target on Windows
description: Qt on Windows treats any existing path ending in .lnk as a shortcut: QFileInfo isFile(), size() and canonicalFilePath() describe the shortcut's target. AttachmentFiles::cachedAt() therefore reports a correctly cached .lnk attachment as unavailable when its target is a folder, missing, offline, empty or larger than the attachment limit, so Retry and readAsync fail with 'The saved attachment is unavailable or changed'. storeAt() no longer writes through shortcuts (fixed with the concurrent-store change). Possible fix: never let a cached name end in .lnk (for example append '_'), or size-check the opened handle instead of QFileInfo for such names, and add a cached()/readAsync assertion to cachedShortcutNeverWritesThroughToItsTarget.
close_reason: Cached attachment names never end in .lnk, a dot or a space, avoid Windows device names, and fit 240 bytes and 180 units while keeping the extension. Downloads, file drops, staging and the composer judge a Windows .lnk as the file QFile reads (tray/src/LocalFile.h). New tests fail on the old sources on Windows and pass on the new ones.

title: Sweep legacy desktop staging folders and require the repository live update for agents
description: Follow-up to zerus-scsy. (3) Earlier ad-hoc updates left hidden .zerus-* staging folders and old hgs-tray.app copies in ~/Applications and ~/.local/bin; let the live update remove only known legacy patterns that are empty folders or GUI copies no process runs, after unregistering bundles from LaunchServices. (4) Add an AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md rule: update local installations only with install.sh, tray/install.sh and mac-install.sh (live GUI replacement through tray/update-installed.py) and never stage GUI copies by hand.
close_reason: Done: tray/update-installed.py removes hidden .zerus-* and stale .hgs-tray-update-* folders beside the GUI after a successful update when they are at least an hour old, hold only installer copies (hgs-tray, hgs, hgs_state.py, hgs-tray.app) and no process runs from or sits in them; macOS bundles are unregistered from LaunchServices first. AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md require the repository installers and a check of other sessions' builds before replacing a running GUI.

title: macOS recovery LaunchAgent respawns every 10 s while a detached worker holds the lock
description: Observed 2026-10-12 on a Mac: com.hgdev.hgs-recovery showed no PID and 'spawn scheduled' with over 1,800 runs, each exiting 0, while an 'hgs recovery worker' started by ensure_worker() (setsid, parent launchd) held recovery/worker.lock. worker() returns 0 when the lock is taken, and KeepAlive=true with ThrottleInterval=10 relaunches it indefinitely. Recovery itself works, but the managed job never owns the worker and wastes a process spawn every 10 s. The race appears after a service restart (kickstart -k) when any hgs invocation spawns a detached worker first. Consider waiting for the lock in the managed worker, having a detached worker yield to the service, or KeepAlive on unsuccessful exit only. Check whether Linux systemd (Restart policy) can loop the same way.
close_reason: Merged in PR #110: the recovery service's worker waits holding a service lock instead of exiting; detached workers yield. Confirm on a Mac after the next install.

title: Kimi: an unchanged model/effort request is reported as not confirmed and blocks later input

Found with a keyless single-model fixture; the desktop picker normally sends only a changed selection. Reject an unchanged request before typing, or accept the native 'Already using' confirmation.
close_reason: Fixed in 358e241: Kimi 2.1 status lines are read by matching the session model's slot (display name with overrides), so an unchanged request is confirmed without typing and real model/effort changes are confirmed; the model picker walk handles the non-wrapping 2.1 list. Verified on real Kimi 2.1.1.
